plugins.description: Right-to-left display for Persian chat messages in the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI — a DSH plugin/bundle (per-block bidi auto-detection, no app file changes)
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-fa-rtl

**Right-to-left display for Persian (Farsi) chat messages in the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI.**

[فارسی](README.fa.md) | English

Persian answers from the model — and your own Persian messages — render right-to-left and right-aligned, while English paragraphs, code blocks, and tables keep their original left-to-right layout. It is a pure DSH plugin: no modification to the application's files, no build toolchain, nothing to configure after install.

## How it works

Every chat row DSH ships is laid out left-to-right (LTR); Persian text inside it is bidi-reordered by the Unicode algorithm, but the *base direction* stays LTR — so Persian paragraphs stay left-aligned and punctuation drifts to the wrong edge.

The web-standard fix is `dir="auto"`. Since plugins cannot touch the React-rendered DOM, this plugin uses its exact CSS equivalent:

```css
unicode-bidi: plaintext;
text-align: start;
```

`unicode-bidi: plaintext` (CSS Writing Modes 4) lets **each text block** choose its own direction from the block's first strong character — a paragraph starting with Persian renders RTL and right-aligns; a paragraph starting with English is unchanged. Consequences:

- Mixed answers (Persian prose + code + tables) render correctly: prose RTL, `<pre>` code deliberately untouched (stays LTR), table cells per-cell, list markers flip with their list.
- The selector scopes only to stable `data-*` attributes that `dsh-client-ui-chat` emits on its flow items (`data-chat-flow-kind`, `data-chat-group-part`, `data-turn-process-answer`). Build-time hashed class names are never referenced, so the plugin survives UI updates. If an attribute ever changes, the CSS simply stops matching — it cannot break the app.

## Install

Requires DSH ≥ 0.2.0-rc.2 with a web composition (`desktop` or `web` profile). Any Chromium/Electron ≥ 105 works.

### From the DSH Web UI

Open the **Plugins** page in the sidebar and install the bundle from this repository's GitHub address (`github:mehdinikzad68/dsh-fa-rtl`). Installation runs `pnpm` in the profile directory and enables the bundle by default.

### From the CLI

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:mehdinikzad68/dsh-fa-rtl
# or, for the web profile:
dsh plugin --profile web add github:<owner>/dsh-fa-rtl
```

Installation normally enables the bundle automatically; if not, toggle it on from the Plugins page. Restart the app once if your profile applies patches only at startup.

### From an agent session

Ask the agent to use the `plugin_manager` tool with action `install_bundle` and the GitHub spec. Each management call requires your approval.

### Local development (no installation)

Clone the repo and point a profile patch row at the **module file** (ESM cannot import a directory). In `<profile-dir>/cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: fa-rtl
      name: 'C:\path\to\dsh-fa-rtl\lib\index.js'
```

## Verify

1. Ask the model something in Persian — the Persian text renders RTL and right-aligned; numbers and punctuation sit correctly; code stays LTR.
2. Browser console (or DevTools) shows: `[dsh-fa-rtl] active — Persian chat text now renders right-to-left`
3. `<head>` contains a `<style data-plugin="dsh-fa-rtl">` tag.
4. Settings → Plugins shows no synchronization error for the bundle.

## Uninstall

Remove the bundle from the Plugins page or with `dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove dsh-fa-rtl` (installed route), or delete the `fa-rtl` insert block from `cordis.patch.yml` (local route). The module system removes the plugin's stylesheet when the entry is disabled.

## Package layout

```
dsh-fa-rtl/
├── package.json        # manifest: dsh.bundle.patch + dsh.client declaration
├── cordis.patch.yml    # bundle patch: registers the fa-rtl Loader row on install
├── lib/index.js        # Host half (Node): imports cleanly, mounts as a Cordis plugin
├── lib/client.js       # Client half (browser): hand-written DSH client bundle, injects CSS
├── README.md / README.fa.md
└── LICENSE             # MIT
```

## Extend

- Want more surfaces RTL (e.g. `ask_user_question` cards)? Widen the scope selector list in [`lib/client.js`](lib/client.js) and save — HMR hot-swaps the bundle, or restart once.
- Want *forced* RTL for everything (even English text)? Replace `unicode-bidi: plaintext` with `direction: rtl` in the same file.

## Known limitations

- A paragraph that *starts* with a Latin word (e.g. «VS Code را نصب کن») resolves LTR in auto mode — the same behavior as `dir="auto"` everywhere on the web; the Persian runs inside still order correctly.
- Overflowing wide tables keep their physical margins; very wide Persian tables may align slightly differently.
- Question cards (`ask_user_question`) and some side bars are intentionally out of scope for v1.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

plugins.description: Runtime evidence that helps agents trace, profile, and burn down hotspots in application and native code, GPU kernels, and inference stacks.
plugins.readme_text:
flameox

Bounded local runtime evidence for coding agents.

Flameox coordinates profilers, benchmark tools, trace processors, and direct local targets. It turns an explicit artifact or command into bounded evidence while keeping durable preservation optional. The agent chooses hypotheses and experiments; Flameox records observed inputs, execution provenance, typed evidence, coverage, and limitations. There is no workspace to initialize or project configuration to maintain. Pass exact artifact paths to analysis and an explicit argv plus absolute working directory to capture. Flameox does not search parent directories, edit project files, or provide a hosted service. ## Quick start Configure an MCP client with the global setup command: ```console npx flameox@latest setup ``` Setup detects supported clients and asks which configurations to update. For automation, select clients explicitly, for example `--client codex --yes` or `--all --yes`; `--dry-run` reports the paths and actions without writing. Setup preserves unrelated client configuration and does not change project files. See [the npm package guide](npm/README.md) for details. Update existing MCP registrations with: ```console npx flameox@latest update ``` `update --check` reports available updates without changing configuration. Updates preserve each client's provider extras and settings, verify the new environment before changing release pins, and report which clients need a restart or reconnect. Use `--client codex` to select one client, or `--version 0.2.8` to select a specific release, including for rollback. The Python CLI exposes the same `flameox update` command. For direct CLI use, pass exact artifact paths or an explicit command: ```console uvx flameox analyze preview_artifact /absolute/path/to/artifact.json uvx flameox capture --provider direct --cwd "$PWD" -- python benchmark.py ``` To launch the stdio MCP server manually: ```console uvx flameox mcp serve ``` For local development, clone the repository, install its development dependencies, and inspect the available tools: ```console git clone https://github.com/morluto/flameox.git cd flameox uv sync --extra dev --extra memory --extra trace --extra cpu uv run flameox mcp inspect ``` ## Evidence and storage Analysis and unpreserved capture use bounded session scratch. Session `analysis_id` values expire when evicted or when the server stops. Explicit preservation creates the user-level Flameox data directory and stores native bytes and a canonical evidence bundle by SHA-256. Set `FLAMEOX_DATA_DIR` to choose another location. Preservation is optional; it does not imply full console-output retention. Flameox distinguishes observed, derived, and inferred claims. Profiles guide exploration but do not establish causality or performance improvement. Confirmatory claims require representative workloads, declared metrics and estimands, compatible identities, preserved samples, and a semantic oracle. ## MCP The MCP server has no workspace binding. It exposes named analysis and capture tools through the same operation registry as the CLI. Analysis tools accept explicit sources; capture tools accept a typed target and provider. Tool schemas expose operation-specific fields directly. Inspect the catalog with `flameox mcp inspect`; use `--tool TOOL_NAME` for focused schemas and examples. The complete contract and current tool catalog are in [the interface guide](docs/interfaces.md). Tools return their full bounded results inline, including failures and recovery actions. Preserved evidence has a durable `evidence_id`; `inspect_evidence` returns its redacted metadata and replay sources inline. Capture takes argv, not a shell string. A direct target supplies an absolute working directory and bounded environment overrides. Results may include `next_page`; replay its named analysis tool and arguments unchanged. Capture continuations read collected artifacts and do not rerun the target. MCP work belongs to the live request, so cancellation applies directly and no detached job survives a restart. ## Documentation - [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) describes process and package boundaries. - [Storage and evidence](docs/storage-and-evidence.md) defines preservation and provenance. - [Investigations](docs/investigations.md) covers experiments, comparison, and evidence quality. - [Adapters](docs/adapters.md) documents provider compatibility and integration policy. - [Runtime safety](docs/runtime-safety.md) covers limits, recovery, integrity, and privacy. - [Interfaces](docs/interfaces.md) defines CLI and MCP contracts. - [Testing](docs/testing.md) describes test selections and known proof gaps. ## Development Flameox requires Python 3.12 or newer and uses the committed `uv.lock`. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for development setup and contribution guidance. ```console uv run ruff check src tests tools uv run ruff format --check src tests tools uv run mypy src tests tools uv run pytest -q ``` Flameox is licensed under the MIT License.

plugins.description: Custom video startup intro for DeepSeek Harness: import clips, tune playback, cross-fade into the workbench, follows the app light/dark appearance.
plugins.readme_text:
# DSH Startup Intro · 启动开场动画 给 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) 加一个可自定义视频的启动开场：导入自己的视频素材，选中哪段，之后每次启动就播哪段；片段、速度、亮度、画面适配、影院填充、展示比例与淡出时长都能调，支持实时预览；播完交叉淡出，直接过渡到工作台。动画还会**跟随 DSH 的浅色 / 深色外观自动选版**。 A video-powered boot intro plugin for DeepSeek Harness: import clips, keep per-clip playback settings, preview live in Settings, then cross-fade into the workbench at every launch. Ships with a procedurally generated demo intro (dark & light cuts). ![启动开场](docs/boot.gif)

## 功能 - **视频素材库**：导入本地视频（`mp4` / `webm` / `mov` 等 Chromium 能解码的格式），删除、切换选中；每段素材各自保存一套参数。 - **启动即播**：直接播放原视频（不做 GIF 转换、不重新编码），播完约 0.8–1.2s 交叉淡出露出 DSH 界面；播放中可点击「跳过开场」。 - **参数调节**：起始位置、播放时长、播放速度、亮度、画面适配（铺满 / 完整）、影院填充（用同一段视频的模糊背景补满画面）、展示比例（播到哪一刻开始淡出）、淡出时长、静音。 - **实时预览**：设置页内嵌预览随参数即时变化；「播放完整开场效果」可在全屏跑一遍完整启动流程。 - **深浅色自动切换**：跟随 DSH 的外观（`body[data-ds-dark-theme]`）自动选择深色版 / 浅色版同一素材；设置页预览也会随外观实时换版。 - **数据都在本机**：素材与参数保存在 `~/.dsh/startup-intro/`，卸载插件不会删除素材。 ## 安装 先确认 `dsh` 可用（DeepSeek Harness 自带 CLI，Electron 桌面版安装目录 `resources/runtime/cli/bin/dsh.cmd`）。 ### 方式一：目录安装（推荐） ```bash git clone https://github.com/zoe1nan/dsh-startup-intro.git dsh plugin --profile desktop add /path/to/dsh-startup-intro ``` ### 方式二：打包安装 ```bash pnpm pack # 或 npm pack，得到 dsh-startup-intro-1.1.0.tgz dsh plugin --profile desktop add /path/to/dsh-startup-intro-1.1.0.tgz ``` > 若 pnpm 报 `[ERR_PNPM_UNKNOWN] ... open '.../pnpm/store/...'`，改用目录安装即可绕过（本地 link 依赖）。 安装完成后**重启 DeepSeek Harness**（Electron 桌面版重启才会加载新 bundle）。打开 设置 → 启动开场 即可看到插件页面。 ## 使用 1. 设置（`Ctrl+Alt+,`）→ 左侧「启动开场」。 2. 点「导入视频」，选择本地视频；导入后自动选中，下次启动就播放它。 3. 调整参数——右侧预览实时生效；点「播放完整开场效果」可在全屏看完整流程。 4. 右上「每次启动播放」可临时关闭开场；「恢复默认参数」重置当前素材。 ## 预置演示素材 `demo/` 下是两段程序化生成的示例开场（1920×1080 / 8.8s / 30fps，各 2–3 MB）： | 文件 | 用途 | | --- | --- | | `demo/startup-intro-dark.mp4` | 深色外观版：深蓝夜空 + 轨道环 + 原生小蓝鲸 | | `demo/startup-intro-light.mp4` | 浅色外观版：纸面蓝墨 + 同构图的墨色鲸 | 一键写入本机素材库并选中： ```bash node tools/seed-demo.mjs ``` 也可以直接在设置页「导入视频」里选这两个文件。生成源码见 `demo/source/intro-art.html`（`?t=` 可定位到任意帧，`&theme=light` 输出浅色版）。 ## 深浅色自动切换 素材条目支持可选的 `lightFile` 字段（同一素材的浅色版）： ```jsonc // ~/.dsh/startup-intro/state.json { "version": 1, "enabled": true, "selectedId": "v9f2b7c4e1a8d3605c7be", "videos": [ { "id": "v9f2b7c4e1a8d3605c7be", "name": "DEEPSEEK HARNESS 开场.mp4", "file": "v9f2b7c4e1a8d3605c7be.mp4", "lightFile": "v9f2b7c4e1a8d3605c7be-light.mp4", "meta": { "duration": 8.8, "width": 1920, "height": 1080 }, "params": { "start": 0, "duration": 8.8, "speed": 1, "brightness": 1, "fit": "cover", "cinema": true, "holdRatio": 0.83, "fadeMs": 1200, "muted": true } } ] } ``` 把浅色版文件放进 `~/.dsh/startup-intro/media/`，并在对应条目加上 `lightFile` 即可：深色外观播 `file`，浅色外观播 `lightFile`。不填 `lightFile` 时两种外观播放同一文件。 ## 实现 ``` index.js Host 半边：状态 / 上传 / 删除 / 媒体直出路由 client.js Client 半边：启动浮层（shell.overlay）+ 设置页（settings.section） cordis.patch.yml bundle 挂载声明 locale/{zh,en}.json 设置页导航与插件卡片的标题 / 描述 icon.svg 插件图标 demo/ 示例开场素材与生成源码 tools/seed-demo.mjs 把 demo 素材写入本机素材库 ``` - Host：`ctx.webServer.register({ kind: 'prefix', path: '/startup-intro' })` 提供 `GET/POST /api/state`、`POST /api/upload`、`POST /api/delete`、`GET /media/`（支持 `Range` / 206）。 所有请求都会先过 `connection.requestRejection(req)`，未授权直接 401。 - Client：`ctx.slots.inject('shell.overlay', ...)` 注册启动浮层（`createPortal` 到 body，保证盖过启动弹窗）； `ctx.slots.inject('settings.section', ...)` 注册设置页。用 `MutationObserver` 监听 `body[data-ds-dark-theme]` 切换素材版本。 - 不使用插件 Config 字段：素材与参数放 `~/.dsh/startup-intro/state.json`，由设置页自己读写。 ## 开发与调试 不想污染现有 profile 时，可以起一个独立测试实例： ```bash # 用内置模板建一个独立 profile（与 desktop 隔离） dsh introtest --from-default-profile web --dump-config dsh plugin --profile introtest add /path/to/dsh-startup-intro # 启动测试实例（--no-open 不弹窗，输出带 token 的调试 URL） dsh introtest --no-open --port 63411 # 用完清理 rm -rf ~/.dsh/profiles/introtest ``` - 改 `client.js` / `index.js`：刷新页面即可生效（客户端 bundle 每次加载时重新取）。 - 改 `package.json` / `cordis.patch.yml`：需要重启实例。 示例开场的生成源码在 `demo/source/intro-art.html`：纯 canvas 2D 程序化动画，`?t=<毫秒>` 可定格任意帧，`&theme=light` 输出浅色版。逐帧截图后再用 ffmpeg 编码即可（仓库未附渲染脚本，按你的环境选 Edge headless / Playwright）。 ## 兼容性 - DeepSeek Harness 桌面版（Electron，web profile）实测；Web 版同理，需注意浏览器自动播放策略（默认静音即可自动播放，取消静音后可能被拦截）。 - 视频解码走 Chromium 内置解码器：H.264/AAC 的 mp4 在桌面版可播；是否支持 HEVC/AV1 取决于 Harness 内置 Chromium 构建。 ## 已知限制 - 桌面端**重启 Harness 后**才加载 / 更新插件（插件在启动时装配，不支持运行中热插拔）。 - 素材保存在本机，不随插件同步；换机器需要重新导入。 - 导入文件大小上限 2 GiB（Host 侧限制）。 ## License MIT

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin: dispatch work to DSH agents from Claude Code / Codex — native subagent progress, in-host worker sessions with per-tier presets, and a multimodal bridge that lends the text-only harness vision and image generation.
plugins.readme_text:
DSH Crew

A DeepSeek Harness plugin: dispatch work to DSH agents from Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok, without giving up the host's native subagent UI.
Native Progress UI • Tier Policy & Escalation • Dispatch Guardrails • Jobs Board • In-Host DSH Sessions • Vision & Image Gen (Native-First) • One-Click Install

npm: @zseven-w/dsh-crew · Current plugin release: 0.1.0-rc.11 · Tested with DSH 0.1.1-rc.1

English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Français · Español · Deutsch · Português · Русский · हिन्दी · Türkçe · ไทย · Tiếng Việt · Bahasa Indonesia


The DSH Crew settings page — host integrations, dispatch policy, execution and the multimodal bridge

## Why DSH Crew DSH Crew is a plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) — an open-source agent harness. It makes DSH agents dispatchable from Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and Grok: the orchestrator keeps its own model, the work runs on a real DSH agent with that harness's tools, sandbox, presets and session history, and the host still shows it as a native subagent with live progress. What runs the work is a DSH agent, not a bare model call. Tiers (`flash` / `pro`) select how much capability that agent gets from the harness's configured roster — DeepSeek V4 Flash and V4 Pro today — so a change of model in DSH needs no change here.
### 🧵 Native Progress UI Workers appear as regular subagents in Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok — dispatch count, running step, tool calls and token usage all show up in the host's own task panel, plus a claude-hud statusline segment: `⚙dsh 1▶pro 2m14s 21.7k/606 ✓3`. ### 🎚️ Tier Policy and Escalation `flash` for mechanical work, `pro` for reasoning, `effort` from `off` to `max`. `tier_policy` can clamp every dispatch to one tier at the tool layer, and `escalate_on_failure` retries a failed flash run once on pro — based on evidence, not on guessing difficulty up front.
### 🏛️ In-Host DSH Sessions With the bundle installed in a DSH profile, each worker is a first-class DSH session: visible in the Web UI, grouped by working directory, mounted with the Agent preset you choose per tier. Without DSH running, dispatch falls back to a standalone DSH runtime, so CI and headless environments still work. ### 👁️ Vision and Image Generation DSH's models are text-only. `describe_image` now prefers DeepSeek's own VL model (`deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp`) whenever a key is available, then falls back to the CLIs you already have — Claude, Codex, Grok, Antigravity — or any OpenAI-compatible API you configure. `generate_image` borrows the same CLIs' brush. Pasted images stay visible in the conversation and reach the model as text.
### 🛡️ Dispatch Guardrails Every dispatch is checked before anything spawns. Worker→worker nesting is capped at origin-chain depth 3 and cycles are refused; a second worker on a workspace another job already holds is refused with the holder's info — never silently queued. Refusals are readable errors: wait or re-scope, don't bypass. ### 📋 Jobs Board The DSH Crew panel doubles as a jobs board: every worker job — running or finished — is listed with tier, effort, live progress and tokens, held workspaces show their holders, and a job that vanishes mid-flight (e.g. a hub restart) is surfaced as an orphan ghost instead of disappearing silently.
### 🔌 Custom Providers Bring your own endpoint (Base URL + API key + models) or a local command template. Each provider has a connectivity test that checks reachability and auth, then makes one real vision call so you find out now, not mid-task. ### 📦 One-Click Install The settings page installs and updates the Claude Code plugin, the Codex role files and the Antigravity / Grok agents, skills and commands for you — marketplace registration, permission allowlist, HUD wiring, absolute paths rendered for this machine — and restores them just as easily. Every settings file is backed up first.
## How it works ``` Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok (orchestrator, keeps its own model) └─ ds-flash / ds-pro ← native subagent shell (progress shows in the host's task UI) └─ MCP: dsh_run_worker(tier, effort, cwd, worker=) ├─ worker="agy"/"grok" → that external CLI runs the task (explicit opt-in) ├─ hub reachable → session inside DSH (visible in the Web UI, grouped by cwd) └─ otherwise → dsh-jsonrpc-agent runtime (worker.cordis.yml) └─ DeepSeek V4 Flash / Pro (DSH SDK, event stream → progress and token stats) ``` ## One run, two views Dispatch fans out. Below, eighteen workers translate this README in parallel: the host counts them as its own subagents, while the harness runs them as real sessions.

Claude Code sees dsh-crew workers as native subagents, with a statusline segment tracking running tiers, elapsed time and tokens.

The DSH Crew panel sees the same run from the harness side: which host dispatched each job, its tier and effort, live progress and token usage.

The panel is also the jobs board: running and finished jobs stay listed with tier, progress and tokens, held workspaces name their holders, and a job that vanishes mid-flight (a hub restart) surfaces as an orphan ghost instead of disappearing silently.

## Install Install into a DSH profile from npm: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add @zseven-w/dsh-crew@latest dsh web ``` Or, for local development straight from the source tree: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-crew dsh web ``` The `link:` protocol symlinks the profile dependency to this repository, so rebuilds are visible immediately. ### Configure DeepSeek credentials (standalone only) In hub mode — the installation above — workers run inside the DSH instance and use the DeepSeek credentials it is already configured with. Nothing else to set up. Only the standalone fallback needs a key of its own: dispatching from a host with no DSH instance running launches a worker runtime as a separate process. Obtain an API key from [platform.deepseek.com](https://platform.deepseek.com) and write it to `~/.config/dsh-crew/.env`: ``` DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=sk-... ``` ### Verify ```bash node scripts/smoke.mjs ``` The smoke test dispatches one cheap job through whichever path is available — the hub when a DSH instance is running, s

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness gate - per-turn persistent-operation counter: remind, instruct the model to stop, then ask for confirmation. Steps aside under sandbox/read-only modes; follows a live permission switch without restart. Verified on real hardware (full -> workspace-write -> read-only -> full). Crafted on an estimated 0.27 USD of model spend.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-confirm-gate

**A bounded-run framework that keeps an AI agent accountable on hosts where you had to grant full permissions.**

English | [中文](README.zh-CN.md) · **v0.1.2**

> **What** — Per-turn counter for persistent operations. Gives the model a brake, not a wall.
> **Verified** — Live hot-switch on Windows (full → workspace-write → read-only → full), no restart. The model stopped itself at 11/15.
> **Cost** — ~$0.27 model spend. Zero external deps, ready-to-install archive in [`dist/`](dist/).
>
> **It steps aside under sandbox / read-only modes** — complementary to DSH's own sandbox, not a replacement.

A runtime plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). It keeps a **per-turn counter of persistent operations**, injects a stop instruction once the free budget is spent, and asks the user for confirmation at a hard limit.

> **Compatibility** — built and verified against DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`; the peer range is `>=0.2.0-rc.2`, so it also loads on `0.2.1-rc.2` and later RC builds. If a future DSH release changes the tool-dispatch hooks this plugin binds to, it will fail loudly rather than silently — see [§7](#7-verifying-the-installation).

> **This is not a security boundary. It is a cost boundary and a course-correction mechanism.**
> It assumes the agent is running **without a sandbox holding the boundary**, and its purpose is to give the model **the ability to brake on its own** before it burns tokens or rewrites files. Real sandbox isolation is provided by DSH's own sandbox — complementary to this plugin, not a replacement.

*Cost figure is an author's estimate — see [`dist/COSTS.md`](dist/COSTS.md). The rest of that day went to environment diagnosis and research, not to this plugin.*

### Scope: it stays silent under a sandbox

The plugin decides, **on every tool call**, whether it should be counting. The mode comes from two sources, in priority order:

1. `ctx.sessionProjections.stateOf(session, 'permissions').sandbox` — the session's **current** knob value. This is what changes when you hot-switch modes mid-conversation.
2. `ctx.shell.sandboxMode` — the executor's **default** mode. Its own documentation calls it "the sandbox mode this executor applies by default"; it does **not** follow a hot switch, so it is only a fallback.

That distinction matters: judged from the default alone, switching into a sandbox and back would leave the plugin reading the value it saw at startup, forever.

Both reads go through `ctx.get(name)`, never `ctx.shell` directly. cordis resolves dependencies lazily, so touching an undeclared service property throws an inject-gate error — and an exception on that path once made the plugin silently do nothing at all. Soft probing cannot throw.

| Sandbox mode | Plugin counts? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `read-only` | ❌ No | The sandbox already holds every boundary |
| `workspace-write` | ❌ No | Same |
| `danger-full-access` | ✅ Yes | Nothing is holding the boundary |
| `custom` | ✅ Yes | A custom mix still leaves the boundary unheld |
| `undefined` / no shell service | ✅ Yes | This executor does not confine |
| **Unreadable (both sources threw)** | ✅ Yes | **Fail open: a silent no-op is worse than an extra reminder** |

That last row is deliberate. This plugin is an accounting tool, not a security boundary, so the two failure modes are not symmetric:

- counting when it shouldn't → a spurious reminder, immediately visible and fixable
- staying silent when it shouldn't → **the plugin appears installed but does nothing**, and nothing in the logs looks wrong

The second is far worse, so any mode it cannot read counts as "not sandboxed".

Put plainly: **under a sandbox this plugin would be redundant — and worse, it would interrupt legitimate operations a second time.** So it steps aside wherever something else is already keeping score.

Hooks are always registered; the decision is per call. That is what makes hot-switching work: move the session into a sandbox and the gate goes quiet on the very next call; move it back and counting resumes. No restart needed.

> ### ✅ Status: verified, including live hot-switching
>
> Exercised by hand on Windows, DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`. The session's permission mode
> was **switched live, without restarting DSH**, walking the sequence
> full → workspace-write → read-only → full:
>
> | Mode | Write a file | `pwsh` | Gate counted? |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | `danger-full-access` | ✅ succeeds | ✅ runs | ✅ **1/10 → 2/10 → 3/10** |
> | `workspace-write` | ✅ succeeds | ❌ fails with `0xC0000142` | ❌ silent (2 ops) |
> | `read-only` | ❌ sandbox denies | ✅ runs | ❌ silent (2 ops) |
> | `danger-full-access` again | ✅ succeeds | ✅ runs | ✅ **1/10, counting resumed** |
>
> Two things matter here. The silent rows show the division of labour working —
> the sandbox confined or rejected the operation and the gate stayed out of the
> way. The last row shows the gate coming back **in the same process**, which is
> the whole point of deciding per call instead of at load.
>
> Honest caveat: in this deployment `ctx.get('shell')` returned `undefined`, so
> the "not sandboxed" verdict came from the *unreadable, therefore fail open*
> branch rather than from a successfully read mode. The behaviour is correct;
> the path is the fallback one. A deployment that exposes `shell` would take the
> primary path instead.

### Who this is for

| Situation | Fits? |
|---|---|
| You granted full permissions and fear unbounded trial-and-error burning tokens | ✅ That is exactly the case |
| You want the agent to ask after N write operations | ✅ |
| You want `read` / `grep` / web lookups **never interrupted** | ✅ Non-persistent operations are never counted |
| You want to use it as a sandbox against a malicious model | ❌ Use DSH's built-in sandbox |
| You use a different agent framework | ❌ This is a DSH plugin |

### Trade-offs & known limitations

Listed first, because they are the interesting part.

1. **The first N operations have no gate at all.** In the default `freeLimit: 10` configuration, operations 1–10 are allowed with only a reminder. That window is deliberate — it gives the model room to correct itself before being asked to stop. Set `freeLimit: 0` when you want zero tolerance; the plugin then ask-confirms before the very first persistent operation.
2. **`confirm` defends against accidents, not injection.** The threat model is a *trusted user with a fallible model*, where the failure to prevent is unbounded trial-and-error. Prompt injection is a different layer — that is what DSH's approval channel and sandbox are for. Do not deploy this as the only thing between an untrusted input and your filesystem.
3. **The release rule is deliberately coarse.** Any message containing the trigger word releases the entire turn, including a message that merely discusses the word. This is on purpose: ambiguity is resolved by what the user typed, not by the plugin guessing intent.
4. **Command judgement is a name comparison, not a parser.** `Get-ChildItem $p.GetFiles()` is counted as persistent, because the plugin does not evaluate the pipeline. The error direction is chosen: over-count, never under-count.
5. **A tool call is one count**, regardless of how many files it touches.

### Why not X

| Alternative | Why not |
|---|---|
| **Hard-block instead of counting** | Tried first in an OpenClaw build. A wall turns every write into an interruption the user did not ask for. With a counter and an explicit stop instruction, the model does the arithmetic itself — it stopped at 11/15 on its own. The brake works better than the wall. |
| **Plugin-only, no DSH host hooks** | The per-turn count has to come from the **tool-dispatch layer**. A wrapper around the model API cannot see individual tool calls, so it cannot count them. The count lives where the calls live. |
| **Fold it into the sandbox** | Different question, different layer. A sandbox answers "is this allowed?". This answers "how much has happened?". Sitting inside the sandbox would tie a budget to a permission model that changes underneath it. |

---

## 1. Design rationale

Granting full permissions is unavoidable — a sandbox makes tools l

plugins.description: DSH 插件：播种 Kimi Coding Plan 供应商，对话输入区底部显示用量（5 小时 / 周 / 月度配额）。
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-kimi-provider

DSH（DeepSeek Harness）插件：为 Web GUI 接入 Kimi Coding Plan（月之暗面 OpenAI 兼容 coding 端点），并附带用量展示。

## 功能

- **provider 播种**：启动时把 `kimi-coding-plan` 路由写入 `llm-pi-ai` 用户设置层——与 Models 页「自定义模型 API」卡片同一条写入路径，按 provider 键合并，与其他插件互不覆盖；模型选择器随即出现 `k3-256k` / `k3` / `kimi-for-coding`（显示名 Kimi-K2.8-Preview）。
- **用量 pill**：会话选用 Kimi 模型时，输入卡片下方显示用量 pill——摘要为 5 小时窗口 / 每周配额百分比（≥90% 标红），点击弹出面板查看各配额已用 / 总量 / 剩余与重置时间。数据取自 Kimi 开放平台。

## 用法

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/youmu129/dsh-kimi-provider
```

1. 配置凭证：在设置页录入 Kimi Console Key（`sk-` 前缀，与模型推理同一把），或设置环境变量 `KIMI_CODING_PLAN_API_KEY`；
2. 重启 `dsh web`，选用 Kimi 模型即见 pill；未配置凭证时 pill 显示「未配置」并给出指引。

可选设置（覆盖 schema 默认值）：`baseUrl`（默认 `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`，海外站用 `https://api.kimi.ai/coding/v1`）、`usage.pollIntervalMs` / `usage.requestTimeoutMs`（默认 0，关闭自动轮询，以手动刷新为主）。

## 开发

```powershell
pnpm install
pnpm run build
pnpm test
```

> API Key 只存放于 DSH 凭证机制或 `apiKeyEnv` 引用的环境变量，不入库、不写入日志与文档。

plugins.description: Independent workspace last-used ordering for the DeepSeek Harness sidebar (experimental)
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-workspace-sorter

Independent **workspace-folder ordering** for DeepSeek Harness, with its own
**Workspace order** section in the existing sidebar View options menu.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-workspace-sorter.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-workspace-sorter)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](./LICENSE)
[![CI](https://github.com/mrbeandev/dsh-workspace-sorter/actions/workflows/check.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/mrbeandev/dsh-workspace-sorter/actions/workflows/check.yml)

- **Source code:** [github.com/mrbeandev/dsh-workspace-sorter](https://github.com/mrbeandev/dsh-workspace-sorter)
- **npm package:** [npmjs.com/package/dsh-workspace-sorter](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-workspace-sorter)

**Contents:** [Why this plugin exists](#why-this-plugin-exists) ·
[Install](#install-from-npm) · [Compatibility](#compatibility-and-limitations) ·
[Development](#build-and-test) · [Local setup](./LOCAL-SETUP.md) · [Release checklist](./RELEASE.md)

## Why this plugin exists

DSH's native **Order by → Last updated** orders sessions inside each workspace,
not the workspace folders themselves. This plugin adds an independent ordering
choice without overwriting the host's saved manual workspace order.

## Install from npm

This checkout prepares **0.1.3**, including the running-workspace folder glow and collapsed-workspace name quick-open. Version 0.1.3 has not been published by this change. Avoid 0.1.0, which failed the isolated GUI boot test.

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-workspace-sorter
```

Disable the older `dsh-workspace-sort` plugin if installed, finish active work,
restart DSH when required, and refresh the actual DSH Web page. Then open
**Workspaces → View options → Workspace order**.

To remove:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-workspace-sorter
```

Restart when required and refresh. No host order needs restoring. Only the
browser preference remains.

## Workspace name quick-open

When a workspace is **collapsed**, clicking its **name** expands it and opens
its latest non-archived session by session update time. Provisional blank
sessions are skipped; an empty workspace simply expands. Clicking the arrow,
folder glyph, or empty row area keeps native expand/collapse-only behavior.
Workspace action buttons are untouched. Clicking the name of an already
expanded workspace keeps native collapse behavior. Modified clicks do not
trigger auto-navigation. This does not change the saved session ordering.

## Running workspace indicator

Workspace folder icons glow **green** while any member session is running,
even when the workspace is collapsed. A selected-but-idle session does not
trigger the glow. Running child agents listed in a member session's subagent
catalog also count. The indicator follows DSH's live session-status store and
clears when the work stops. It works with either workspace-order choice.

The glow is steady (no flashing animation). Only the folder glyph receives
color and shadow; native row selection, labels, and session indicators remain
unchanged. It does not imply a workspace has merely been selected. The
implementation and status aggregation are unit-tested; the full running →
idle transition still needs a real-agent browser test. The sidebar smoke suite
passes with the indicator wrapper installed.

## The Workspace order menu

| Option | Effect |
|---|---|
| **Manual workspace order** (default) | Displays the host's saved manual order. |
| **Last used workspace** | Latest member-session activity first; empty workspaces last and ties in manual order. |

The native session-order choice remains independent. See the limitations below.

> **0.1.3 candidate — not published by this change.** Published 0.1.0 failed real-browser activation in a clean DSH profile; avoid enabling it. The corrected candidate passes 10/10 real-browser smoke checks and 4/4 post-uninstall checks on DSH 0.2.0-rc.2. Broader coexistence and interaction testing remains pending. See [RELEASE.md](./RELEASE.md).

Independent workspace ordering in the DeepSeek Harness sidebar's existing **View options** popup, below its session-order options.

- **Workspace order → Manual workspace order** retains the host's saved order (default).
- **Workspace order → Last used workspace** displays workspaces newest first, by the latest `updatedAt` among their member sessions. Empty workspaces sort last; ties retain manual order.
- Session ordering, grouping, archive filtering, pinning, search, rename and delete remain native.
- Preference is browser-local, persisted as `dsh-workspace-sorter.order.v1`. It synchronizes across tabs on the same origin.
- No network requests, credentials, session contents, or persistent host workspace changes.

## Compatibility and limitations

**Pinned internal adapter for DSH 0.2.0-rc.2.** The native view-options menu has no public extension slot. This plugin wraps the registered `WorkspaceBrowser` function, transforms the returned `ViewOptionsMenu`, and projects a sorted workspace snapshot. It preserves the original entry's injected services, child-slot permissions, locale, and store. It does not edit installed DSH bundles or manipulate the DOM. This is an internal integration, not a stable public menu API; the adapter waits for native registration and leaves unmatched sidebar components untouched rather than failing application boot.

“Last used” is **latest session activity**, not merely clicking a folder. Activity includes archived sessions. Workspace-tree mode keeps the native hierarchy and applies ordering within it. In flat mode there is no workspace list to reorder. Workspace drag commits are suppressed while Last used is active; switch to Manual before dragging. Session drag behavior remains native. The native drag affordance is still shown.

The UI additions are intentionally English-only. Full browser runtime/HMR and coexistence testing is still required before release. A full refresh after enabling/disabling is required because the adapter changes the live component entry; automatic HMR is not claimed.

## Build and test

```sh
npm run check
npm pack
```

An optional installed-bundle shape check runs when `DSH_TEST_WORKSPACE_CLIENT` points to the installed `dsh-client-ui-workspace/lib/client.js` artifact. Without it, that one integration check is skipped so contributors and CI do not need a private DSH installation. This check inspects shape, not browser behavior.

Editable client source is `client/index.mjs`. `scripts/build.mjs` produces `lib/client.js`, using the GUI's React singleton rather than bundling React. Host `index.mjs` is intentionally a no-op; `cordis.patch.yml` registers the dual-face package. No Remote or additional service namespace is required. The sole injected package is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace`, which owns the sidebar and supplies its dependencies.

## Try locally

First test the packed tarball in a disposable web profile. Do not publish without explicit authorization.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add /absolute/path/to/dsh-workspace-sorter-0.1.0.tgz
```

Before activating in your normal profile, **disable the existing `dsh-workspace-sort` plugin** (entry `workspace-sort`): it independently overwrites the host's manual order daily and would undermine the meaning of Manual here. This package does not silently disable another plugin. Restart DSH if requested and refresh the actual DSH GUI. Open Workspaces → View options → Workspace order.

Verify manual/last-used toggling, new session activity, reload persistence, narrow/collapsed sidebar, workspace-tree/flat grouping, archive filters, search, session drag, workspace drag in Manual, and uninstall + refresh. Uninstalling leaves only the browser preference; no host order needs restoring.

# dsh-changelog-zh

从真实 git 历史生成**两份中文变更日志**：

- **用户版（短）**——一段可以直接贴进群公告或 Release 正文的中文说明；
- **开发者版（长）**——每条提交带完整 SHA、分类依据、文件增减、验证证据原文。

两份里的**每一条都带 commit SHA 和「已验证／未验证」标记**。

这个工具的三个承诺，也是它唯一值得存在的理由：

1. **只说历史里有的事。** 分类靠约定式提交前缀和一张小关键词表，识别不出就写「未分类」，绝不猜。
2. **「已验证」必须有可引用的证据。** 四类证据之外，一律标「未验证」，并写清缺的是哪一类。只有一句 `verified: true` 而没有证据的，同样算未验证。
3. **不翻译提交信息。** 你没写中文标题的提交，就原样保留英文主题，并明确告诉你「有 N 条没有中文标题」——不会给你一段看起来很像中文、实际是模型编的文案。

当前版本 **0.1.0**。

---

## 它长什么样

下面是这个工具在本文档末尾描述的演示仓库上的**真实输出**（原文粘贴，未手工润色）：

```console
$ node bin/changelog-zh.mjs --repo tmp/demo-repo \
    --sessions tmp/demo-sessions.jsonl --title v1.1.0 \
    --out tmp/demo-out --no-emails --stdout --format user
```

```markdown
# v1.1.0

2026-10-16 · 共 6 条变更：3 条已验证、3 条未验证。

## 破坏性变更

- ⚠ 换掉返回结构（`1993535`，未验证）

## 新功能

- 支持把结果导出成 Markdown（`182d11c`，已验证）

## 修复

- 修掉导出时的编码问题（`46378b4`，已验证）

## 性能

- 导出时少做一次全量拷贝（`83fb0b5`，未验证）

## 重构

- 拆出渲染层（`4939351`，未验证）

## 未分类

- update the deployment notes（`af2971a`，已验证）

> 范围：v1.0.0..HEAD · 共 6 条变更
> 「未验证」只表示提交历史里没有可引用的验证证据，不代表这条改动有问题。
> 判定依据：提交信息或 git notes 里的验证 trailer（`已验证:` / `Verified:` / `测试:` …），或会话记录里退出码为 0 的验证命令。完整规则见开发者版。
> 其中 1 条没有中文标题，原样保留了提交主题（本工具不翻译提交信息）。
> 生成于 2026-10-16T04:06:07.769Z · dsh-changelog-zh@0.1.0 · 数据来源：git log
```

开发者版里同一条「性能」改动是这么写的（节选）——注意它没有把「匹配到会话记录」当成验证通过：

```markdown
### 4. 导出时少做一次全量拷贝（`83fb0b5`，未验证）

- 提交：`83fb0b584d05a391cd8f8deba0e0c5a6c7665bc4`
- 类型：性能（分类依据：提交前缀 perf）
- 破坏性：否
- 作者：林可
- 提交时间：2026-10-10 10:00
- 文件（1 个，+1 −0）：
  - `src/fast.js` +1 −0
- 提交主题（原文）：perf: 导出时少做一次全量拷贝
- 验证：未验证 —— 匹配到 1 条会话记录，但里面没有退出码为 0 的验证命令，也没有 failed=0 且 passed>0 的测试计数
```

以及「提交信息 + git notes 两处都有证据，就把两句原文都抄下来」：

```markdown
- 验证：已验证 —— 提交信息 trailer「测试：node --test，退出码 0」
- 验证：已验证 —— git notes「已验证：node --test 46 passed」
```

---

## 安装与用法

### 作为 DSH 插件（宿主路由 + 会话面板 + 工具）

本插件是零依赖的纯 JS 包，把仓库挂进 DSH 的插件目录即可（`dsh.bundle.patch` + `dsh.client` 已声明）：

```yaml
# cordis.patch.yml（本仓库自带）
- insert:
    - id: dsh-changelog-zh
      name: dsh-changelog-zh
```

装上以后有三个入口：

- **会话面板**：对话视图里的「变更日志」标签页，填仓库/范围/会话记录即可生成，可一键复制；
- **HTTP 路由**：`GET /dsh-changelog-zh/state`、`POST /dsh-changelog-zh/generate`、`POST /dsh-changelog-zh/clear`；
- **工具**：`changelog_zh`，参数 `{ repo, range, since, limit, includeMerges, sessions, format }`，`format` 取 `user` / `dev` / `both`。

插件配置（都可选）：

```jsonc
{
  "roots": [],            // 路径白名单；非空时只允许生成这些目录下的仓库
  "defaultRepo": "",      // 请求没给仓库时用哪个
  "defaultRange": "",     // 默认范围，如 "v1.0.0..HEAD"
  "sessionsPath": "",     // 会话记录文件
  "titlesPath": "",       // 中文标题映射文件
  "maxCommits": 300       // 单次最多读多少条提交
}
```

### 作为命令行工具

```console
$ node bin/changelog-zh.mjs --repo D:\Projects\某项目 --title v1.1.0
已写入 D:\Projects\某项目\CHANGELOG-user.md  —— 用户版（短）
已写入 D:\Projects\某项目\CHANGELOG-dev.md  —— 开发者版（长）
范围 v1.0.0..HEAD · 6 条提交 · 已验证 3 · 未验证 3 · 已隐去 0 处 · 会话记录匹配 2 条
```

全部参数：

| 参数 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| `--repo <路径>` | 仓库路径，默认当前目录 |
| `--range <范围>` | 如 `v1.0.0..HEAD`、`HEAD~5..HEAD`；不写则自动（见下） |
| `--since <日期>` | 只取该日期之后的提交，如 `2026-10-01`、`"2026-10-01 09:00"` |
| `--limit <条数>` | 最多读多少条提交（默认 300，上限 5000） |
| `--merges` | 把合并提交也算进来（默认不含） |
| `--sessions <文件>` | 叠加会话记录（格式见下） |
| `--titles <文件>` | 中文标题映射 JSON，形如 `{"<完整或短 sha>": "中文标题"}` |
| `--title <标题>` | 覆盖两份文案的标题 |
| `--format user\|dev\|both` | 只产出其中一版（默认 `both`） |
| `--out <目录>` | 输出目录，默认仓库根目录 |
| `--stdout` | 同时打印到标准输出 |
| `--json` | 把完整报告打成 JSON 到标准输出（不写文件） |
| `--no-authors` / `--no-emails` | 开发者版里隐去作者／邮箱 |
| `-h` / `-v` | 用法 / 版本 |

退出码：`0` 成功、`2` 参数错误、`1` 生成失败（错误码写在 stderr，如 `[ENOTREPO]`）。

**自动范围**：没有标签时取最近提交；有标签时取 `最近标签..HEAD`；如果最新标签已经在 HEAD 上（刚打完标签就要写 Release notes 的典型场景），自动回退到**上一个**标签，避免把这次已发布的提交再写一遍。范围是怎么定的，开发者版会写在「范围」那一行里。

---

## 「已验证／未验证」到底怎么判

只有下面四类**可引用证据**存在时，才会标「已验证」：

| # | 证据 | 例子 | 抄进文案的内容 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 提交信息里的验证 trailer | `Verified: node --test → 46 passed` | 原句 |
| 2 | git notes 里的验证 trailer | `git notes add -m "测试：node --test，退出码 0"` | 原句 |
| 3 | 会话记录里退出码为 0 的验证命令 | `{"command":"node --test","exitCode":0}` | 命令 + 退出码 |
| 4 | 会话记录里 `failed=0` 且 `passed>0` 的测试计数 | `{"tests":{"passed":46,"failed":0}}` | 计数 |

trailer 的键名认这些（大小写不敏感、中英都行）：`verified` / `verified-by` / `verify` / `verification` / `tested` / `tested-by` / `test` / `tests` / `evidence` / `check` / `checked` / `已验证` / `验证` / `自测` / `测试` / `测试结果` / `测试通过` / `证据`。写成 `**已验证**：…` 这种加粗形式也认得。

两条**从严**的例外，请特别注意：

- **通过与失败并存 ⇒ 未验证。** 如果同一提交既有一句 `Verified:`，又有一条退出码非 0 的测试记录，本工具按「未验证」处理，并在文案里写明「存在失败的验证证据」。宁可保守。
- **声称 ≠ 证据。** 会话记录里只有 `"verified": true`、却没给命令/退出码/计数的，依旧标「未验证」，理由写成「声称已验证但没有证据」。

反过来，「未验证」**不代表改动有问题**——它只表示提交历史里没留下能引用的证据。这条也会印在每一份用户版文案的页脚里，免得被读者误读。

本工具**不会**从「改了测试文件」「diff 很大」「提交信息写得很详细」这类形状去推断验证结论。

---

## 脱敏

渲染之前先脱敏，命中即替换为 `<已隐去:类型>`，并在文案里报出命中数量：

GitHub token（`ghp_` / `gho_` / `ghs_` / `ghu_` / `ghr_` / `github_pat_`）、`sk-` 类 API key、Slack token、AWS access key id、JWT、`Bearer …`、私钥块（`-----BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY-----`）、带密码的连接串、`password: xxx` / `token: xxx` 这类赋值、以及本机用户路径（`C:\Users\…` 与 `C:/Users/…` 两种写法）。仓库根目录与 origin 地址在进入报告前也会过一遍脱敏。

一个真实例子：一条提交信息里写了 `token ghp_***`，用户版和开发者版里都只会出现 `<已隐去:github-token>`，页脚写「已在生成时隐去 1 处疑似凭据或本机用户路径」。

---

## 会话记录格式

这是一个**约定的摘要文件**，不是 DSH 内部会话库的格式。支持 JSON 数组、单个 JSON 对象，或 JSONL（`#` 开头是注释，空行忽略）：

```jsonl
{"commit":"182d11c","title":"支持把结果导出成 Markdown","commands":[{"command":"node --test","exitCode":0},{"command":"npm run lint"}],"tests":{"passed":46,"failed":0}}
{"commit":"af2971a","verification":{"command":"node --test","exitCode":0,"evidence":"46 passed"}}
```

- `commit`：完整 sha、唯一前缀（≥4 位）或短 sha 都能匹配；**有歧义就进「歧义清单」，不猜**；
- 匹配不上的记录进「未匹配清单」，开发者版会列出记录与原因；
- `title` / `titleZh`（也认 `summary`）用作中文标题来源，优先级低于 `--titles` 映射、高于提交 trailer；

匹配上**不等于**已验证：记录里必须有上面第 3、4 类证据。

---

## 它不做什么

- **不联网**，不调用任何模型 API；除 `git` 只读命令外不执行别的进程；**不写任何文件**（CLI 的 `--out` 除外）。
- **不改仓库**：不发提交、不打标签、不写 notes。
- **不翻译、不推断**（见上文三个承诺）。
- **不解析 DSH 内部会话库**：会话记录只认上面这个约定格式。
- 合并提交默认不进日志（要就加 `--merges`）；空提交与合并提交在开发者版里会写「文件：无（可能是空提交或合并提交）」，不会假装它有改动。

---

## 参考了什么、有什么不同

本工程是**独立实现**，没有 fork、没有克隆任何人的仓库、没有拷贝任何第三方代码。

**骨架**照的是本机另一个自己写的 DSH 插件工程 `dsh-warden`（同一作者）：零依赖 `scripts/build.mjs`（`src/*.js` → `lib/`）、`cordis.patch.yml` 描述片段、宿主半区 + 客户端半区 + `test/*.test.mjs` 的布局、`scripts/wrap-client.mjs` 的 `window.__ModuleLoader__` 包装方式、`.gitattributes` 的 LF 约定。差异在于职责完全相反：warden 是在工具调用**之前**拦一层，本插件是读 git 历史**之后**产出一段文案；因此本插件没有 `rules.js`/`classify.js` 那套判定流水线，而是 `git → classify → evidence → redact → render` 这条只读链路，并且附带一个可独立运行的 CLI。

**生态定位**（下面两条事实来自 GitHub API 返回的仓库公开描述，我没有读它们的源码，本工程不含它们任何代码）：

- [`7dgroup-ai/dsh-skill-7d-git-commit`](https://github.com/7dgroup-ai/dsh-skill-7d-git-commit)：公开描述是「在生成任何 `git commit` 提交信息前，自动按 7DGroup 项目提交规范进行校验」。它管的是**提交信息的规范**（写之前）。
- [`andyfan1094/dsh-github`](https://github.com/andyfan1094/dsh-github)：公开描述是「GitHub authentication and local Git workflow plugin for the dsh web GUI」，是账号认证与本地 Git 工作流面板。

两者都不产出「从真实变更生成一份敢公开的中文文案」。本插件补的就是这一环。需要说明的是，这个「生态里没人做」的判断来自上面两条公开描述，不是穷尽调研——如果你知道已经有同类插件，欢迎在 issue 里告诉我。

同样地，本工程**故意没有** `screenshots.json`、没有伪造的面板截图：作者没有把插件装进自己的 DSH 配置里跑过面板渲染，所以不给不存在的截图。面板行为由 `test/host.test.mjs` 里的宿主契约测试覆盖（路由前缀、状态码、工具 schema、卸载），而不是靠图片证明。

---

## 开发

```console
$ node scripts/build.mjs          # src/*.js -> lib/（host.js -> index.js），并内联客户端 CSS
$ node --test test/*.test.mjs     # 全部测试
```

- 零运行时依赖，`devDependencies` 为空；只需要 Node ≥ 22 与 `git`。
- `lib/` 是入库的构建产物，`test/build.test.mjs` 会逐字节比对 `lib/` 与 `src/`，改了源码忘了构建会直接红。
- 测试里凡是涉及 git 的都**真的建临时仓库**（`test/helpers/repo.mjs`），不 mock git；本机没有 `git` 时这些用例自动 skip 并说明原因。
- CI（`.github/workflows/ci.yml`）在 Node 22 / 24 上跑构建一致性 + 全部测试 + CLI 冒烟。

DSH Crew

A DeepSeek Harness plugin: dispatch work to DSH agents from Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok, without giving up the host's native subagent UI.
Native Progress UI • Tier Policy & Escalation • Dispatch Guardrails • Jobs Board • In-Host DSH Sessions • Vision & Image Gen (Native-First) • One-Click Install

npm: @zseven-w/dsh-crew · Current plugin release: 0.1.0-rc.11 · Tested with DSH 0.1.1-rc.1

English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Français · Español · Deutsch · Português · Русский · हिन्दी · Türkçe · ไทย · Tiếng Việt · Bahasa Indonesia


The DSH Crew settings page — host integrations, dispatch policy, execution and the multimodal bridge

## Why DSH Crew DSH Crew is a plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) — an open-source agent harness. It makes DSH agents dispatchable from Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and Grok: the orchestrator keeps its own model, the work runs on a real DSH agent with that harness's tools, sandbox, presets and session history, and the host still shows it as a native subagent with live progress. What runs the work is a DSH agent, not a bare model call. Tiers (`flash` / `pro`) select how much capability that agent gets from the harness's configured roster — DeepSeek V4 Flash and V4 Pro today — so a change of model in DSH needs no change here.
### 🧵 Native Progress UI Workers appear as regular subagents in Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok — dispatch count, running step, tool calls and token usage all show up in the host's own task panel, plus a claude-hud statusline segment: `⚙dsh 1▶pro 2m14s 21.7k/606 ✓3`. ### 🎚️ Tier Policy and Escalation `flash` for mechanical work, `pro` for reasoning, `effort` from `off` to `max`. `tier_policy` can clamp every dispatch to one tier at the tool layer, and `escalate_on_failure` retries a failed flash run once on pro — based on evidence, not on guessing difficulty up front.
### 🏛️ In-Host DSH Sessions With the bundle installed in a DSH profile, each worker is a first-class DSH session: visible in the Web UI, grouped by working directory, mounted with the Agent preset you choose per tier. Without DSH running, dispatch falls back to a standalone DSH runtime, so CI and headless environments still work. ### 👁️ Vision and Image Generation DSH's models are text-only. `describe_image` now prefers DeepSeek's own VL model (`deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp`) whenever a key is available, then falls back to the CLIs you already have — Claude, Codex, Grok, Antigravity — or any OpenAI-compatible API you configure. `generate_image` borrows the same CLIs' brush. Pasted images stay visible in the conversation and reach the model as text.
### 🛡️ Dispatch Guardrails Every dispatch is checked before anything spawns. Worker→worker nesting is capped at origin-chain depth 3 and cycles are refused; a second worker on a workspace another job already holds is refused with the holder's info — never silently queued. Refusals are readable errors: wait or re-scope, don't bypass. ### 📋 Jobs Board The DSH Crew panel doubles as a jobs board: every worker job — running or finished — is listed with tier, effort, live progress and tokens, held workspaces show their holders, and a job that vanishes mid-flight (e.g. a hub restart) is surfaced as an orphan ghost instead of disappearing silently.
### 🔌 Custom Providers Bring your own endpoint (Base URL + API key + models) or a local command template. Each provider has a connectivity test that checks reachability and auth, then makes one real vision call so you find out now, not mid-task. ### 📦 One-Click Install The settings page installs and updates the Claude Code plugin, the Codex role files and the Antigravity / Grok agents, skills and commands for you — marketplace registration, permission allowlist, HUD wiring, absolute paths rendered for this machine — and restores them just as easily. Every settings file is backed up first.
## How it works ``` Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok (orchestrator, keeps its own model) └─ ds-flash / ds-pro ← native subagent shell (progress shows in the host's task UI) └─ MCP: dsh_run_worker(tier, effort, cwd, worker=) ├─ worker="agy"/"grok" → that external CLI runs the task (explicit opt-in) ├─ hub reachable → session inside DSH (visible in the Web UI, grouped by cwd) └─ otherwise → dsh-jsonrpc-agent runtime (worker.cordis.yml) └─ DeepSeek V4 Flash / Pro (DSH SDK, event stream → progress and token stats) ``` ## One run, two views Dispatch fans out. Below, eighteen workers translate this README in parallel: the host counts them as its own subagents, while the harness runs them as real sessions.

Claude Code sees dsh-crew workers as native subagents, with a statusline segment tracking running tiers, elapsed time and tokens.

The DSH Crew panel sees the same run from the harness side: which host dispatched each job, its tier and effort, live progress and token usage.

The panel is also the jobs board: running and finished jobs stay listed with tier, progress and tokens, held workspaces name their holders, and a job that vanishes mid-flight (a hub restart) surfaces as an orphan ghost instead of disappearing silently.

## Install Install into a DSH profile from npm: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add @zseven-w/dsh-crew@latest dsh web ``` Or, for local development straight from the source tree: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-crew dsh web ``` The `link:` protocol symlinks the profile dependency to this repository, so rebuilds are visible immediately. ### Configure DeepSeek credentials (standalone only) In hub mode — the installation above — workers run inside the DSH instance and use the DeepSeek credentials it is already configured with. Nothing else to set up. Only the standalone fallback needs a key of its own: dispatching from a host with no DSH instance running launches a worker runtime as a separate process. Obtain an API key from [platform.deepseek.com](https://platform.deepseek.com) and write it to `~/.config/dsh-crew/.env`: ``` DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=sk-... ``` ### Verify ```bash node scripts/smoke.mjs ``` The smoke test dispatches one cheap job through whichever path is available — the hub when a DSH instance is running, s

plugins.description: 抓虾数据插件｜DeepSeek Harness（DSH）CSV / Excel / JSON 预览、数据概览、筛选去重、排序转换与表格导出。独立运行，无需抓虾后端。
plugins.readme_text:
# 抓虾数据插件 · DeepSeek Harness（DSH）CSV / Excel / JSON

**简体中文** | [English](README.en.md) · [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) · [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/howtimeschange/dsh-crawshrimp-data/releases) · [DSH Plugin topic](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin)

抓虾数据工具是面向 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）的独立本地数据插件，可在 DSH 进程内预览、统计、清洗和导出 JSON、CSV、Excel（XLSX）数据。它适合商品表检查、库存汇总、订单数据整理，以及把浏览器或脚本产物转换成新的表格文件。无需安装抓虾应用或后端，也不需要抓虾 API Token、Python 运行时或其他配套插件；这是独立社区项目，不是 DeepSeek 官方插件。

## 快速开始

需要 Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`，以及已验证的 DSH **0.2.1-alpha.4**。通过 GitHub Release 安装预打包版本，或直接安装带 JavaScript 产物的 GitHub 标签：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile ecommerce add -w github:howtimeschange/dsh-crawshrimp-data#v0.2.1
DSH_DATA_WORKSPACE=/absolute/path/to/data dsh --profile ecommerce --dump-config
DSH_DATA_WORKSPACE=/absolute/path/to/data dsh --profile ecommerce
```

无需执行包构建脚本。也可以克隆仓库后执行 `npm ci`，再安装本地目录：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile ecommerce add -w /absolute/path/to/dsh-crawshrimp-data
```

`DSH_DATA_WORKSPACE` 指定插件使用的工作目录；未指定时默认使用 DSH 启动目录。也可以在 profile patch 中覆盖完整配置：

```yaml
- id: crawshrimp-data
  config:
    workspaceDir: /absolute/path/to/data
```

详细安装方式见 [官方 bundle 安装文档](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/user/develop/basic/publish.md)。项目通过 GitHub 分发，未假定已经发布到 npm 注册表。

## 能力概览

| 工具 | 能力 |
| --- | --- |
| `crawshrimp_data_preview` | 读取 JSON、CSV、XLSX，选择工作表，按页返回最多 100 行 |
| `crawshrimp_data_profile` | 统计缺失值、不同值数量，以及数值列的最小值、最大值、合计和均值 |
| `crawshrimp_data_export` | 将 JSON 记录写入新的 CSV 或 XLSX 文件；不会覆盖已有文件 |
| `crawshrimp_data_transform` | 声明式筛选、去重、排序、选列和重命名；可只预览或保存新文件 |

文件读取和写入限定在配置的 `workspaceDir`。写文件使用 DSH 原生审批信号：当会话同时处于 `danger-full-access` 且原生审批策略为 `never` 时，已有完全权限授予，插件不会重复请求逐次审批；其他状态继续走原生审批路径，无法获得审批时故障关闭。插件不会覆盖已有文件，同一插件实例的会话共享该工作目录。

## 使用示例

可以直接对 DSH 说：

> 预览 `products.xlsx`，统计缺失价格和库存，然后把选定记录导出到 `products-clean.csv`。

工具调用可以传入 JSON 记录：

```json
{
  "path": "products-clean.csv",
  "rows": [
    { "sku": "A001", "price": 39.5, "stock": 8 },
    { "sku": "A002", "price": 60.5, "stock": 0 }
  ]
}
```

将该对象交给 `crawshrimp_data_export`，再用 `crawshrimp_data_profile` 读取 `{"path":"products.xlsx"}`。以零开头的货号必须传为 JSON 字符串，例如 `"00123"`。CSV 导出会为可能被表格软件识别为公式的文本（含表头）加前置单引号；XLSX 文本保持字面值。

## 商品表清洗与脚本衔接

JSON 输入可以是记录数组，也可以是脚本产物 `{ "success": true, "data": [...] }`。明确声明 `success: false` 的失败产物会被拒绝。记录必须由扁平标量字段组成；`001` 等标识符作为字符串保持原样。JSON 的 `null` 与空字符串在内部保持区别，CSV/XLSX 写入时 `null` 表示空单元格。空数组可以通过 `{ "columns": [...], "data": [] }` 声明表头。

调用 `crawshrimp_data_transform` 可以使用以下计划：

```json
{
  "path": "products.json",
  "filters": [{ "column": "stock", "op": "gt", "value": 0 }],
  "dedupeBy": ["sku"],
  "sortBy": [{ "column": "price", "numeric": true, "direction": "desc" }],
  "columns": ["sku", "price", "stock"],
  "rename": { "sku": "product_id" }
}
```

不传 `outputPath` 时只计算预览、行数和统计；加上 `"outputPath": "products-clean.xlsx"` 或 `.csv` 路径后，才会通过原生权限检查保存新文件。处理顺序固定为：筛选 → 去重（保留第一条）→ 排序 → 选列/重命名。计划中的列名都指输入列；不执行表达式、SQL 或 JavaScript。即使结果为零行，只要声明了表头，也会生成带表头的文件。`crawshrimp_data_export` 的 `rows` 为空时必须提供 `columns`。

筛选条件按 AND 组合：`eq`、`ne`、`contains`、`in`（传 `values`）、`gt`、`gte`、`lt`、`lte`、`is_empty`、`not_empty`。相等比较保留类型差异；CSV 单元格读出为字符串。数值比较只接受有限十进制数或对应字符串，不解析带货币符号的文本。排序默认按文本比较；要按数值排序请设置 `numeric: true`，空值和无法解析的数值排在最后。最多 20 个筛选条件和 5 个排序键。转换预览最多返回 20 行和 256 KiB，并明确报告是否截断；保存文件包含完整的有界结果。示例见 [`examples/sample-products.json`](examples/sample-products.json) 和 [`examples/transform-products.json`](examples/transform-products.json)。

## 范围与限制

- 输入支持不超过 10 MiB 的 JSON、UTF-8 CSV 和 XLSX；表格最多 10,000 行、200 列、200,000 个单元格，列名最多 256 个字符，表头必须非空且不重复。
- 导出输入最多 5 MiB JSON，单元格最多 10,000 个字符；普通预览最多返回 100 行且结果不得超过 512 KiB。
- XLSX 公式单元格只使用已保存的缓存值，没有缓存值时返回标记；公式和宏不会执行。日期不会在 CSV 与 XLSX 之间自动统一。
- XLSX 解析前会限制 ZIP 条目数量和展开大小。超出边界时会明确报错，不会静默截断大型数据。
- 目录约束是常规本地路径和软链接检查，不能替代防御其他进程并发修改软链接的操作系统沙箱。
- 插件不编辑已有复杂工作簿，不重算公式、不渲染图表，也不连接卖家账号或商家系统。

仓库的 `npm test` 覆盖真实中文 CSV/XLSX 往返、数值统计、公式文本、路径与软链接越界、拒绝覆盖、取消、实际 Cordis/DSH ToolRuntime 中的注册/审批/卸载，以及完全权限、`ask`、受限策略和审批服务缺失/异常时的权限映射。插件不调用模型 API，也不需要真实商家账号。

## 相关插件

[浏览器插件](https://github.com/howtimeschange/dsh-crawshrimp-browser) · [Office 插件](https://github.com/howtimeschange/dsh-crawshrimp-office)。浏览器、数据和 Office 插件分别安装、可以独立运行；网页脚本和翻页能力归浏览器插件。

MIT。能力设计来自抓虾的本地产物处理流程，运行实现直接使用独立 Node 库。

## 版本说明

0.2.1 对齐 DSH 原生完全权限策略：`danger-full-access` 与 `never` 同时成立时不重复请求审批；其他状态继续走原生审批并在无法获批时故障关闭。0.2.0 新增 JSON 产物直读和声明式表格转换；0.1.0 标签已被替代。

# 🛡️ dsh-permission-rules - **1024 store channel**: `npm i -g dsh1024` once, then `dsh1024 plugin --profile web add dsh-permission-rules` (counts toward the [deepseek1024.com](https://deepseek1024.com) install ranking). [![Gitee](https://img.shields.io/badge/Gitee-mirror-c71d23?logo=gitee)](https://gitee.com/perrylink/dsh-permission-rules) [![dshfind](https://dshfind.com/api/badge/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules?metric=downloads)](https://dshfind.com/plugins/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules?ref=badge) [![OpenSSF Scorecard](https://api.securityscorecards.dev/projects/github.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/badge)](https://api.securityscorecards.dev/projects/github.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules) **Claude Code-style declarative permission rules for DeepSeek Harness.** *Rules decide what is known. A reviewer model decides what is not.* [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![DSH plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/dsh--plugin-✅-green)](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin) [![dsh-doctor](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PerryLink/dsh-plugin-doctor/main/badges/PerryLink__dsh-permission-rules.svg)](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-plugin-doctor#verified-徽章) [![DSH Market](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/2BingLing/dsh-market/master/assets/readme/badge-top-rated.svg)](https://dsh.market/) [![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%5E22.19%20%7C%7C%20%3E%3D24-brightgreen.svg)](#) [![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/ci.yml?branch=main&label=CI)](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/actions) [![Version](https://img.shields.io/github/v/tag/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules?label=version)](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/releases) [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-permission-rules)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-permission-rules) [![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/dsh-permission-rules)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-permission-rules) [English](README.md) · [简体中文](README-zh.md) · [Español](README-es.md) · [Português](README-pt.md) · [हिन्दी](README-hi.md)
--- **📖 Ecosystem knowledge base** — measured data, not marketing: [plugin development guide · plugin-selection data · maintenance criteria](https://perrylink.github.io/dsh-plugin-guide/). ## ⭐ 如果它帮到了你 这个插件是 [DSH 插件家族](https://github.com/PerryLink)的一员（40+ 个，全部 Apache-2.0）。如果你在用，**给个 star** —— 它不会解锁任何功能，但会让下一个人在搜索里更容易找到它。 *English:* part of a 40+ plugin family for DeepSeek Harness. If it is useful, **a star helps the next person find it** — nothing is gated behind it. ## What is dsh-permission-rules? Claude Code-style declarative permission rules for DeepSeek Harness. Rules decide what is known. A reviewer model decides what is not. ![Terminal demo of dsh-permission-rules: dsh-permission-rules — deny/ask rules in one YAML file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/main/docs/assets/dsh-permission-rules-demo.png) ![Animated terminal demo of dsh-permission-rules](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/main/docs/assets/dsh-permission-rules-demo.gif) *The same run, animated.* ## Compatibility | Surface | Status | |---|---| | Harness | DeepSeek Harness `dsh-v0.2.1-alpha.1` (adapted 2026-09-22, full gate chain): its plugin config is the live settings contract — every field is declared `.volatile()`, the Loader hands `apply` a live reference per field, and a saved edit is committed into the running references WITHOUT remounting the plugin, with out-of-range values refused by the schema before anything is written. A host whose Schemastery predates `volatile()` (before 3.18.3) still mounts and runs this plugin — the fields simply stay ordinary values and the live config form is unavailable — because the marker is applied through a capability probe rather than assumed. `Session.append` on this line still cannot stamp the `ignorable` marker (its third argument is the surface-intent bag, and the envelope field survives for stored-log reads only), so the whole `0.2-alpha` line is pre-checked as unmarked and session-log audit stays disabled by default — `append` reads only `sourceEventSeqs`/`surfaceOp` and freezes the envelope, so it has no code path that could stamp the marker; the earlier `0.1.7-alpha` (adapted 2026-09-22), `0.1.5-rc.2` (adapted 2026-09-09) and `0.1.3-alpha` lines keep the same surface-only append signature, and every `0.2` prerelease is classified with them (a STABLE `0.2.x` release is left to the append probe, so a restored marker surface is adopted without a new plugin release). Those lines' log migrations refuse unclassified plugin events even when marked, so `strip` v1 audit rows before a `0.1.3-alpha` host opens the log and v2 audit rows before a `0.1.5-alpha` host migrates it (native v3 logs only need `repair`). | | Node | `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` | | Platforms | All (host + web settings client) | | Model | Any (deny/ask reasons surface through tool results) | ## What you get `dsh-permission-rules` puts an ordered **`allow` / `deny` / `ask`** rule list in front of every tool call on the `tools/pre-execute` waterfall — deterministic, instant, auditable, and written by you in plain YAML: - **`deny`** blocks the call; the rule's `reason` becomes the model-visible error. - **`ask`** rides the official approval seam (mount `dsh-auto-review` for a second-model answerer, or a human answers; with neither, the harness fails closed). - **`allow`** (and no-match) strictly delegates via `next()` — downstream listeners are never short-circuited. Every hit **and** every passthrough is audit-logged as a `permissionRules/decision` session event (log-only — nothing extra is injected into the model context). - **Rich matching** — tool-name globs (including `mcp__*`), agent-identity selectors (`main` / `subagent` / `preset:*`), argument key/value globs **or** regexes (with `!pattern` negation and an `absent` key dimension), workspace-relative path globs at **any nesting depth**, `when` host conditions (env vars, platform), and **shell command decomposition** (`argv`: command word, argument tokens, pipeline signature) for token-precise command matching. - **Built-in high-risk baseline** — a shipped deny/ask ruleset (destructive commands, privilege escalation, download-and-execute, sensitive paths) enabled by default and appended after user rules so a nearer user rule can override it; toggle with `builtin.enabled`. - **Hierarchical rule files** — optional `searchUp` merges every `.dsh/rules.yaml` from the session cwd to the filesystem root, nearest first. - **Dry-run rollout** — `enforce: false` audits what the policy *would* do while passing every call through. - **Hot reload** — Chokidar watch with debounce; a broken edit keeps the previous rules, never crashes. On a WSL host, or for a rule file under `/mnt/`, the watch switches to polling because native change events are unreliable there. - **Fail loud** — invalid YAML, unknown actions/fields, bad globs/regexes, backtracking-prone patterns, or more than `maxRules` rules fail the load. ## Rule syntax ```yaml # /.dsh/rules.yaml rules: - match: { tools: [bash, pwsh], params: { command: "git push*" }, paths: ["**/secrets/**"] } action: deny reason: "No pushes from protected paths" - match: { tools: [edit, write] } action: ask reason: "File writes need confirmation" ``` - **Match dimensions** — `tools` (globs, incl. `mcp__*`), `agents` (`main` / `subagent` / `preset:`; unknown identity never matches — fail closed), `params` (key/value globs or regexes, `!pattern` negation, `absent` key dimension), `paths` (workspace-relative globs extracted at any nesting depth), `when` (`env` var globs/regexes + a closed `platform` list), and `network` (`domains` / `ips` / `ports` / `schemes` — globs, wildcards, CIDRs, port ranges). - **Actions** — `allow` / `deny` / `ask`, evaluated in file order, first match wins. - **Rule metadata** — `enabled: false` (visible but inert), `description`, `tags`; unknown fields fail the load. - **Schema**
