# Opencode Connect (`dsh-plugin-opencode-connect`)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![DeepSeek Harness Plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/DeepSeek%20Harness-Plugin-blueviolet?logo=deepseek)](https://www.deepseek.com/en/harness/) [![OpenCode Desktop](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCode-Desktop%20Free%20Models-2ea44f?logo=opencode)](https://opencode.ai) [![GitHub Repository](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Dreftian%2FOpencode--Connect-black?logo=github)](https://github.com/Dreftian/Opencode-Connect) [![Status: Production Ready](https://img.shields.io/badge/Status-Production%20Ready-success)](https://github.com/Dreftian/Opencode-Connect) **Seamlessly connect and dynamically auto-sync all OpenCode Desktop free models into DeepSeek Harness.** [English Documentation](#english) • [Documentación en Español](#español)
--- ## 🇬🇧 English Documentation ### 📌 Overview & The Problem It Solves **DeepSeek Harness** is a high-performance orchestration framework and desktop workspace for advanced AI agents, multi-step reasoning, and software development workflows. However, developers often face friction with paywalled APIs, rate limits, credit-card requirements, or complex authentication setups for secondary models. **OpenCode Desktop** provides an extensive, curated suite of free LLM models optimized for coding, reasoning, long-context analysis, and multimodal tasks. **OpenCode Connect (`dsh-plugin-opencode-connect`)** bridges this gap: - **Zero API Keys Required**: Seamlessly leverages your existing local OpenCode Desktop instance. - **10+ Free Pre-Configured Models**: Instantly exposes high-capability free models into DeepSeek Harness with no billing or subscription requirements. - **Dynamic Auto-Synchronization**: Automatically monitors and syncs models whenever OpenCode Desktop updates its model registry, changes configurations, or introduces new free models—with zero restarts required. - **Native DeepSeek Harness Streaming**: Full integration with Cordis and DeepSeek Harness protocols, featuring real-time token streaming and reasoning/thinking traces (`thinking_delta` & `text_delta`). --- ### 🧠 Supported OpenCode Desktop Free Models The plugin automatically discovers and maps the complete catalog of free models from OpenCode Desktop: | Model ID | DeepSeek Harness Name | Context Window | Thinking / Reasoning | Modality | Best For | | :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- | | `opencode/beam-free` | Beam Free [Free] | 32,768 | ❌ | Text | Ultra-fast responses, linting, concise edits | | `opencode/big-pickle` | Big Pickle [Free] | 65,536 | ✅ | Text | Balanced algorithmic coding & problem solving | | `opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` | DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Free [Free] | 131,072 | ✅ | Text | High-throughput code synthesis & agent planning | | `opencode/glm-5.3-flash-free` | GLM-5.3-Flash Free [Free] | 131,072 | ✅ | Text | Deep reasoning, multilingual translation, code review | | `opencode/longcat-2.5-preview-free` | LongCat 2.5 Preview Free [Free] | 262,144 | ❌ | Text | Massive context comprehension, full-repo analysis | | `opencode/mimo-v2.6-flash-free` | MiMo-V2.6-Flash Free [Free] | 131,072 | ✅ | Text | Low-latency chat & reactive interactive agents | | `opencode/nemotron-3-ultra-free` | Nemotron 3 Ultra Free [Free] | 65,536 | ✅ | Text | Enterprise code analysis & complex architecture | | `opencode/nemotron-3.5-lightning-free` | Nemotron 3.5 Lightning Free [Free] | 65,536 | ❌ | Text | Instant snippet generation & documentation | | `opencode/nemotron-3.5-super-vl-free` | Nemotron 3.5 Super VL Free [Free] | 65,536 | ✅ | Text, Image | UI/UX mockups, visual debugging, charts | | `opencode/space-bunny-free` | Space Bunny Free [Free] | 65,536 | ✅ | Text | Creative engineering, prompt design, test suites | --- ### 🔄 Dynamic Auto-Synchronization Engine ```mermaid flowchart LR A["OpenCode Desktop
(Local Service / CLI)"] <-->|"opencode models
Periodic Discovery"| B["OpenCodeModelSynchronizer
(Background Daemon)"] B -->|"Event: models-updated"| C["OpenCodeAdapter
(LlmAdapter)"] C -->|"Dynamic Registration"| D["DeepSeek Harness
LLM Runtime"] D -->|"Stream Requests / Thinking Blocks"| E["Agent & Chat Sessions"] ``` 1. **Auto-Discovery on Boot**: On initialization, `OpenCodeModelSynchronizer` invokes `opencode models` via standard local CLI paths across Windows, macOS, and Linux. 2. **Differential Comparison**: Keeps a snapshot of known models and computes differences. If OpenCode rolls out a new model version or introduces a new free tier model, the synchronizer emits a `models-updated` event. 3. **Hot Registry Refresh**: DeepSeek Harness updates its active provider catalog dynamically. Users can immediately select newly added models in the dropdown selector without reloading the application. --- ### 🚀 Installation Instructions for DeepSeek Harness #### Method 1: Via DeepSeek Harness GUI (Recommended) 1. Open **DeepSeek Harness Desktop**. 2. Click on **Complementos** (Plugins) in the left navigation sidebar. 3. Click the **+ Agregar complemento** (+ Add Plugin) button in the upper right. 4. In the text field, paste the official GitHub repository URL: ```text https://github.com/Dreftian/Opencode-Connect ``` *(Alternatively, you can provide the package name `dsh-plugin-opencode-connect` if published, or the path to a local directory).* 5. Click **Instalar** (Install). DeepSeek Harness will install the plugin and automatically detect your OpenCode Desktop models. --- #### Method 2: Via DeepSeek Harness CLI / Cordis Patch Using the DeepSeek Harness CLI toolchain: ```bash # Using pnpm pnpm dsh plugin add dsh-plugin-opencode-connect # Or using npm npm install --save dsh-plugin-opencode-connect ``` Or apply the included bundle patch in your `cordis.patch.yml`: ```yaml - insert: - id: llm-opencode-connect name: dsh-plugin-opencode-connect ``` --- #### Method 3: Local Directory Path Installation (Development / Offline) To run or develop from source: ```bash # Clone the repository git clone https://github.com/Dreftian/Opencode-Connect.git cd Opencode-Connect # Install dependencies and build npm install npm run build ``` Then in DeepSeek Harness GUI: 1. Navigate to **Complementos** > **+ Agregar complemento**. 2. Select **Cargar desde directorio local** (Load from local folder) or paste the absolute path: ```text C:\Users\\path\to\Opencode-Connect ``` 3. Click **Confirmar**. --- ### ⚙️ Configuration Options Configuration can be specified in your Cordis / DeepSeek Harness configuration file (`cordis.yml` or plugin options): ```yaml dsh-plugin-opencode-connect: # Path to opencode or opencode-cli executable. # Leave empty ("") to auto-detect across standard installation paths. cliPath: "" # Background synchronization polling interval in milliseconds. # Default: 30000 (30 seconds) syncIntervalMs: 30000 # Filter only free models provided by OpenCode Desktop. # Default: true onlyFreeModels: true # DeepSeek Harness LLM provider prefix ID. # Default: "opencode" providerPrefix: "opencode" # Human-readable provider display name. # Default: "OpenCode Desktop" providerDisplayName: "OpenCode Desktop" # Enable streaming of internal reasoning/thinking tokens. # Default: true enableThinking: true # Per-request execution timeout in milliseconds. # Default: 180000 (3 minutes) timeoutMs: 180000 # Diagnostic log level ('debug' | 'info' | 'warn' | 'error'). # Default: "info" logLevel: "info" ``` --- ### 🛠️ Troubleshooting & Diagnostics #### 1. "OpenCode CLI binary not found" - **Cause**: OpenCode Desktop might be installed in a custom non-standard directory, or not yet launched. - **Solution**: - Ensure **OpenCode Desktop** is installed and has been run at least once so it extracts its CLI helper. - Specify the explicit binary path in your config (`cliPath: "C:\\path\\to\\opencode-cli.exe"` or `/usr/local/bin/opencode-cli`). - Standard auto-detected locations: - **Windows**: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\@op

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin: semantic search over the AGENTS.md and README.md rules of your workspace tree, with a tool for the agent and a command for you.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-regras

Semantic search over the Markdown rules of a directory tree, inside
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).

`AGENTS.md` and `README.md` are where an agent learns how a repository works.
`dsh-regras` indexes those files with [memsearch](https://github.com/zilliztech/memsearch)
and gives the agent a tool to find the rule that applies to the task in front of
it, with the real file path and line range so it can open the source. A command
adds a hygiene report: duplicate candidates, path references that no longer
exist, and docs that stopped while the code moved.

One plugin line, two surfaces:

| Who | How | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| the agent | `qual_regra` tool | the rule segments for the task, with the **real path** and line range |
| you, in the chat | `/regras [higiene \| pares \| buscar <termo>]` | the hygiene report or a rule search |

## Requirements

- **Node.js** `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` (the same range DeepSeek Harness supports).
- **pnpm** on `PATH`; the harness manages profile plugins with it.
- **DeepSeek Harness** itself, e.g. `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web`.
- **memsearch** for the index, with the local ONNX embeddings extra:
  `uv tool install "memsearch[onnx]"` (or `pipx install "memsearch[onnx]"`).

The `qual_regra` tool is plain Node.js. The `/regras` hygiene report is a bash
plus Python script (`relatorio.sh` calls `relatorio.py`), so it runs on Linux and
macOS; on Windows, run it from WSL or Git Bash with Python available.

## Install

```sh
# 1. pnpm (needed by `dsh plugin`)
npm install -g pnpm

# 2. add the plugin to your `web` profile
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add github:songjongdevsecops/dsh-regras

# 3. restart the harness: the bundle layer is read at boot
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web
```

If `dsh` is already installed globally, step 2 is
`dsh plugin --profile web add github:songjongdevsecops/dsh-regras`.

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so `dsh plugin add` appends
`dsh-regras` to `dsh.profile.bundles` in the profile manifest. That line is the
only activation, and it is applied at every boot.

Check the loaded line:

```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep -A3 regras
```

Expected shape:

```yaml
- id: regras
  name: dsh-regras
  config: {}
```

### Update and uninstall

```sh
# update: re-run the add command, then restart the harness
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-regras   # uninstall, then restart
```

## Build the index

`dsh-regras` reads an existing memsearch collection; it does not embed anything
itself. Index the tree that holds your rules once:

```sh
memsearch index ~/workspaces -c regras-bgem3-v1
memsearch stats -c regras-bgem3-v1
```

The command indexes every Markdown file below the tree. If you want only
`AGENTS.md` and `README.md`, give `memsearch index` a directory that contains
just those files (a symlink mirror works). The plugin resolves each hit through
`realpath`, so the answer always cites the real file, not the mirror.

The collection name is the contract between the index and the plugin: it defaults
to `regras-bgem3-v1` and is configurable on both sides.

## Configuration

Every path is configurable and the defaults derive from your home directory, so
nothing is tied to a specific machine. Override by environment variable, or by
the config of the `regras` line in your profile patch. A patch replaces the
whole config of the line, so restate every key you want to keep.

| Config key | Environment variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `raiz` | `DSH_REGRAS_RAIZ` | `~/workspaces` | root of the rules tree |
| `colecao` | `DSH_REGRAS_COLECAO` | `regras-bgem3-v1` | memsearch collection |
| `memsearch` | `DSH_REGRAS_MEMSEARCH` | `~/.local/bin/memsearch` | memsearch binary |
| `espelho` | `DSH_REGRAS_ESPELHO` | `<package>/.espelho`, else `raiz` | corpus scanned by the hygiene report |

The report also uses `DSH_REGRAS_PY` (a Python interpreter with `pymilvus` and
`numpy`); by default it uses the memsearch tool environment, then `python3`.

Profile patch example (`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`):

```yaml
- id: regras
  config:
    raiz: '/home/you/rules'
    colecao: 'regras-bgem3-v1'
    memsearch: '/home/you/.local/bin/memsearch'
    espelho: '/home/you/rules'
```

## Usage

Ask the agent a question about where something belongs, how to name it, what is
forbidden, or who owns it. It calls `qual_regra` and gets the matching segments
with their source paths.

In the chat:

```sh
/regras buscar naming          # five best rule segments
/regras higiene                # duplicate candidates, orphan paths, doc/code drift
/regras pares                  # the candidate pairs, with both texts, for review
```

`higiene` writes `relatorios/<date>-higiene/` next to the package, with
`relatorio.md` and `pares-candidatos.jsonl`. The duplicate line is **candidates
only**: embeddings measure topical proximity, not contradiction, and two
opposite rules look alike in the vector space. The reader decides with both
texts in hand. Nothing is rewritten: the report only reads files.

## Verification

From a clone of the repository:

```sh
node --test tests/
python3 scripts/relatorio.py --selftest
```

The test suite covers the tool and command registration, real-path resolution,
secret-path rejection and the package contract. The report selftest covers path
citation, orphan detection, git drift and kNN. Neither needs the index.

To verify the install, check the `dump-config` output above and ask the agent
for a rule.

## Troubleshooting

- **`binário não encontrado: memsearch`** — install memsearch or point
  `DSH_REGRAS_MEMSEARCH` at the binary.
- **No results** — the collection is empty or has another name. Run
  `memsearch index <tree> -c <name>` and make the names match.
- **Report says `pymilvus indisponível`** — the interpreter running the report
  has no `pymilvus`. Set `DSH_REGRAS_PY` to the memsearch environment Python
  (`~/.local/share/uv/tools/memsearch/bin/python`) and restart the harness, or
  run `DSH_REGRAS_PY=<that-python> bash scripts/relatorio.sh` directly.
- **`pnpm not found on PATH`** — `npm install -g pnpm`, then re-run.
- **Plugin installed but nothing appears** — restart the harness; the bundle
  layer is read at boot, not at install time.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

plugins.description: Codex-style file-based long-term memory for DSH: two-stage extraction, consolidated MEMORY.md handbook, prompt-injected summary, and search/read/list/note tools.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-codex-memories

Codex-style **long-term memory** for DSH: cross-session memory that ingests finished sessions, consolidates them into a searchable handbook, and injects a compact summary before every turn.

It reproduces the two-stage structure of the Codex memory system rather than approximating it: per-session extraction first, then a consolidation pass over many raw memories.

## Why

DSH sessions are isolated by default. A correction you made yesterday, a command that only works in one repo, a symptom/cause/fix you already paid for — none of it carries over unless you restate it. This plugin makes the agent remember:

- how you want it to work, without being told twice
- where the truth lives in a specific repo, and which commands actually run
- which failure has which fix

## How it works

```
session goes idle for N seconds
   └─ Stage 1  one model call per session -> session_summaries/<slug>.md + raw_memories.md
        └─ Stage 2  once enough memory accumulates -> MEMORY.md + memory_summary.md
             └─ before each turn, memory_summary.md is injected into the prompt
```

All durable artifacts are plain Markdown you can read, edit, version, or move. `index.json` holds the extraction cache, job records, and the consolidation watermark.

## Install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add @lushdawn/dsh-codex-memories
```

Local development:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add link:<absolute path to this directory>
```

Restart DSH, or let a live profile hot-load it.

## Commands

| Command | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `/memory status` | memory root, extracted sessions, pending consolidation, last timestamps |
| `/memory show` | print the current `memory_summary.md` |
| `/memory extract` | extract the current session immediately |
| `/memory backfill` | scan stored sessions and extract the ones never processed |
| `/memory consolidate` | merge pending memory into `MEMORY.md` now |
| `/memory forget <sessionId\|all>` | drop extraction records (handbook content is kept) |
| `/memory on` / `off` | toggle automatic extraction for this process |

## Tools

Exposed to the model when `dedicatedTools` is on:

| Tool | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `memory_search` | line-level keyword search across memory files (`any` / `all` / `on_same_line`) |
| `memory_read` | read one memory file by line range |
| `memory_list` | inventory of the memory folder and pending work |
| `memory_note` | append one ad-hoc note — the only write path the model is offered |

The model is instructed to cite memory as `MEMORY.md:12-14|note=[...]`.

## Configuration

Every field has a safe default; override in your profile patch:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: dsh-codex-memories
      name: dsh-codex-memories
      config:
        storageDir: ''            # default $DSH_HOME/memories
        generate: true
        use: true
        dedicatedTools: true
        model: ''                 # e.g. deepseek-official/deepseek-flash
        extractModel: ''          # falls back to model
        consolidationModel: ''    # falls back to model
        idleSeconds: 120
        maxSessionsPerRun: 3
        maxSessionAgeDays: 30
        consolidationThreshold: 2
        maxInjectChars: 9000
        minSessionMessages: 4
        extractMaxTokens: 8000
        consolidateMaxTokens: 16000
```

When `model` is empty the plugin reads the current default model, then falls back to `deepseek-official/deepseek-flash`.

## Data layout

```
$DSH_HOME/memories/
├── MEMORY.md                    # durable handbook, Task Group organized
├── memory_summary.md            # prompt-loaded layer; first line must be v1
├── raw_memories.md              # mechanical stage-1 merge, ascending session id
├── session_summaries/<slug>.md  # one structured recap per session
├── extensions/ad_hoc/notes/     # notes written by you or the model
└── index.json                   # extraction cache, job records, watermark
```

## Cost and privacy

- **It spends tokens**: one Stage-1 call per session and one Stage-2 call per consolidation. Sessions under 4 messages are skipped; at most 3 sessions are processed per sweep.
- **Local files only**: no network access beyond the model API it calls.
- **It enters your prompt**: `memory_summary.md` is injected every turn, which is why it is capped by `maxInjectChars`.
- **Auditable**: every artifact is readable Markdown.
- **The model cannot rewrite the handbook**: it may only append ad-hoc notes; consolidation is a separate pass, so one turn cannot corrupt durable memory.

## Fidelity to Codex

The behavioral spec comes from reverse engineering Codex itself — the on-disk shape under `~/.codex/memories` plus the prompt templates embedded in `codex.exe`:

| Codex | dsh-codex-memories |
| --- | --- |
| `~/.codex/memories/` | `$DSH_HOME/memories/` |
| `MEMORY.md` / `memory_summary.md` / `raw_memories.md` | same names, same formats |
| `rollout_summaries/*.md` | `session_summaries/*.md` |
| `memories_1.sqlite` | `index.json` |
| Stage 1 extraction prompt | `PHASE1_TEMPLATE` in `lib/prompts.js` |
| Phase 2 consolidation prompt | `PHASE2_TEMPLATE` in `lib/prompts.js` |
| usage guidance + citation format | `USAGE_TEMPLATE` in `lib/prompts.js` |
| rollout scan backfill | `/memory backfill` + boot sweep |

See [docs/mechanism.md](docs/mechanism.md) for the full mechanism and the evidence behind it.

## Known limits

- Stage 2 asks for two complete documents in one reply. On a very large handbook the reply can hit the output cap; the old files are then kept and the pass reports an error instead of writing something corrupt.
- Automatic extraction needs the process alive during the idle window; otherwise the next boot's `backfill` catches up.
- Retrieval is keyword/line based, not semantic — the same tradeoff Codex makes. Route with `keywords` in `MEMORY.md`.

## Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome — see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). For anything
security-related, follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) instead of opening a public issue. Release
history lives in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).

## License

MIT

plugins.description: 让你对模型说出“棍母“时模型不再困惑——dsh-ottosmother By DeepSeek-V4.1-flash1017的12,853,598tokens
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-ottosmother

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that gives the model a private glossary: when you
write 「滚木」 it should read it as 「没有」, when you write 「棍母」 it should read
it as 「不存在」, and when it needs to say "there is none" it should phrase the
whole sentence naturally with one of those words instead of mechanically
swapping a single token.

The plugin only adds one **system prompt section**. It does not rewrite user
input, does not wrap model output, and does not register any message hooks.

```
- 「滚木」= 没有
- 「棍母」= 不存在
```

- Reading: 「说了个棍母」→ the user is saying nothing was said; 「这里有滚木」→
  there is nothing here.
- Writing: 「这里没有东西」→ 「这里有棍母」; 「这个功能不存在」→ 「这个功能是棍母」.
- Code, commands, paths, URLs and error text are asked to stay verbatim.

Whether the model actually uses the words is its own judgement — this is a
prompt-level rule, not a hard replacement.

## How it works

| Extension point | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `systemPrompt.section` | Injects the 「固定用语」 section (glossary + reading rules + writing rules + verbatim rule) |

Section name `dsh-ottosmother/glossary`, order 50. The text is produced by a
function and re-read from config on every prompt assembly; when the plugin is
disabled or the term list is empty, the section text is an empty string and
nothing is injected.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-ottosmother
```

Or from GitHub:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:hj9178/dsh-ottosmother
```

Restart the harness after installing.

## Config

Adjust it in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: dsh-ottosmother
      name: 'dsh-ottosmother'
      inject: [systemPrompt]
      config:
        enabled: true
        terms:
          - word: '滚木'
            meaning: '没有'
          - word: '棍母'
            meaning: '不存在'
```

- `enabled`: master switch; when false nothing is injected.
- `terms`: the glossary. `word` is what the user writes, `meaning` is what it
  stands for.

## Known behaviour

- Whether the model writes 「滚木 / 棍母」 is its own decision; it may still say
  「没有」, and it may rewrite when explicitly asked.
- Code is not protected by code — the rule only asks the model to keep it
  verbatim.

## License

MIT.

---

# dsh-ottosmother（中文）

给 DeepSeek Harness 的插件，把一份私人词表写进 system prompt：用户写
「滚木」要理解成「没有」，写「棍母」要理解成「不存在」；模型要表达「没有 /
不存在」时，用这些词把整句改写得自然通顺，而不是机械扣掉两个字再塞一个词。

插件只加一个 **system prompt 段落**：不改用户输入、不包装模型输出、不注册任何
消息钩子。

- **理解用户**：「这里有滚木」→ 理解为「这里什么也没有」；「说了个棍母」→
  理解为「什么也没说」。
- **模型回复**：要表达「没有 / 不存在」时，自己把整句改写通顺，例如
  「这里没有东西」→「这里有棍母」，而不是「这里滚木东西」这种生硬结果。
- 代码、命令、路径、URL、报错信息要求原样保留。

模型是否真的使用这些词，是模型自己的判断——这是提示词层面的规则，不是硬替换。

## 生效方式

| 扩展点 | 做什么 |
| --- | --- |
| `systemPrompt.section` | 注入「固定用语」说明（词典 + 理解规则 + 表达规则 + 代码原样规则） |

段落名 `dsh-ottosmother/glossary`，order 50。文本由函数提供，每次组装 prompt
时现读配置；插件关闭或词表为空时返回空串，等价于不注入。

## 安装

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-ottosmother
```

或从 GitHub 安装：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:hj9178/dsh-ottosmother
```

安装后重启 harness 生效。

## 配置

在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里调整：

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: dsh-ottosmother
      name: 'dsh-ottosmother'
      inject: [systemPrompt]
      config:
        enabled: true
        terms:
          - word: '滚木'
            meaning: '没有'
          - word: '棍母'
            meaning: '不存在'
```

- `enabled`：总开关，关掉后不注入任何内容。
- `terms`：词表，`word` 是用户写的自造词，`meaning` 是它代表的含义。

## 已知行为

- 模型是否用「滚木 / 棍母」表达由模型自己判断，可能偶尔说成「没有」。
- 代码没有被代码保护——规则只是要求模型自己保持原文。

## License

MIT。

plugins.description: Draws mermaid code blocks in DSH replies as diagrams, including while the reply is still streaming.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-plugin-mermaid Draws ```` ```mermaid ```` code blocks in DSH replies as diagrams — **including while the reply is still streaming**.

> dsh-plugin-mermaid — 把回复里的 ```mermaid 代码块画成图表，边流式输出边画
中文说明（点开） —— 不用等一轮回复结束才看到图 **它是什么**：模型在回复里写 ```` ```mermaid ```` 围栏，你看到的是图，不是代码。图上方一条细栏写着 `Mermaid`，右边是 **复制** 和 **源码/图表** 开关。 **为什么不是"等回复结束再画"**：DSH 渲染流式回复时，**已完成的块只解析一次、React 元素被缓存**，每个 token 只重建尾部那一块。所以规则只有一条：**源文本静止 220ms 才画**。token 在流 → 计时器一直被重置 → 什么都不画；围栏一闭、后面的正文开始到达 → 块冻结 → 图立刻出现。模型在围栏里停顿时不会画出半张图。 **复制**：图模式复制一张 PNG（2–3 倍尺寸、铺了代码块自己的底色，粘到文档里就是一张图）；源码模式复制 Mermaid 文本。浏览器剪贴板不收 SVG，所以图是先栅格化再写的 —— 这也是 Mermaid 跑在 `htmlLabels: false` 的原因：`` 里的 HTML 在"SVG 当图片"时会消失。 **认不出来就不画**：Mermaid 解析失败的块原样保留，不插任何东西。 **装法**：Plugin Manager 的 Add plugin 填 `github:kjx-talesofai/dsh-plugin-mermaid#v0.2.1`，或指向本地目录。装完**重启 app**（Host 半边开机才加载资产路由），页面再 **⌘R**。 **它没有做什么**：不改 Markdown 渲染器、不占槽位、不加工具。只在代码块的 `data-code-block-content` 里加一个节点，用一条 `:has()` 规则把源码 `
` 藏起来。
## What it does The model writes a fenced block: ````text ```mermaid flowchart LR A["工作区"] --> B["暂存区"] --> C["仓库"] ``` ```` You see the diagram, under a small bar that names it and offers **源码** (source) and copy. The block's own "Code block" banner is hidden while the diagram is shown, because the plugin never touches the `
` React owns — it
adds a sibling and hides the original with CSS.

**Copy follows the view.** With the diagram on screen the button puts a PNG on
the clipboard (2–3× the drawn size, on the block's own surface colour, so it
pastes into a document without a transparent-background surprise); with the
source on screen it copies the Mermaid text. Browser clipboards will not take an
SVG reliably, so the diagram is drawn through a canvas first — which is also why
Mermaid runs with `htmlLabels: false`: `foreignObject` HTML does not survive that
trip.

## Why this is not a Markdown plugin

There is no slot between "Markdown" and "code block". The only seat a plugin can
take is the whole `assistant-step` node, and taking it would mean re-implementing
Markdown — file links, image lightboxes, KaTeX, syntax highlighting, copy
buttons, sticky banners — to add one block type.

So the plugin decorates the primitive's own markup instead:

```
div.md-code-block
  div.bannerWrap                   ← hidden while a diagram is shown
    div[data-code-block-banner]    ← language label + copy
  div[data-code-block-content]
    pre                            ← the source (left in place, hidden by CSS)
    div.dsh-mermaid                ← the one node the plugin adds
```

The coupling is that markup. `tests/dom.test.mjs` drives a stand-in with the same
shape in a real browser, so a change to it fails loudly here instead of silently
drawing nothing.

## Why streaming needs care

DSH renders a live reply with an incremental Markdown renderer: every completed
block is parsed once and its React elements are cached, so only the growing tail
is re-rendered on each token. That gives one precise rule:

> never draw the tail; draw only a source that has stopped changing.

A block is drawn after its source has been unchanged for 220 ms. While tokens
flow the timer keeps resetting; when the fence closes and the next prose starts,
the block freezes, and the diagram appears mid-reply — no waiting for the turn to
end. A pause *inside* an open fence that lasts longer than 220 ms will draw
whatever has arrived; if the source then keeps growing, the panel is dropped and
redrawn, and a source Mermaid rejects leaves the code block exactly as it was.

Rendered diagrams are cached by source + theme, so a re-render (React rebuilding
the message, a theme switch) costs no Mermaid work.

## Where Mermaid comes from

The browser half asks the Host for `/api/mermaid.asset.js`; the Host serves the
`mermaid.min.js` from this package's own dependency tree over the same
authenticated, same-origin channel as the rest of the Web UI. The build is found
by Node's own resolution (`createRequire`), not by a fixed
`./node_modules/…` path: pnpm — which the Plugin Manager uses — keeps a
package's dependencies *beside* it, so a fixed path would 404 on every install
from Git while working perfectly in a linked checkout. It is a 3.4 MB
script, so it is fetched the first time a diagram is seen, not on every page
load, and revalidated with an ETag.

## Limits

- Diagrams are rendered in the browser only. A DSH client without the plugin (a
  phone on an old tab, `--no-client` tooling) shows the code block.
- Mermaid's `strict` security level is used: HTML labels are sanitized, and
  click-to-activate links are not available.
- A diagram Mermaid rejects is not decorated at all. The reason is logged to the
  browser console (`[mermaid] …`); there is no inline error row, because during
  streaming an incomplete diagram would flash one.
- No per-block history: the panel is a view of the file's Markdown, not a record.

## Install

Use DSH's own **Add plugin** dialog. No npm account, no publishing.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| GitHub | `github:kjx-talesofai/dsh-plugin-mermaid#v0.2.1` |
| Local directory | an absolute path, e.g. `/path/to/dsh-plugin-mermaid` |

Restart the desktop app afterwards: the Host half owns the asset route and is
only loaded at startup. The browser half reloads with the page (`⌘R`).

This plugin is **not published to npm**, and `npm install` is not the install
path. Its one runtime dependency (the Mermaid build the Host serves) is installed
from the repository's `package.json`.

## Tests

```bash
npm ci
npm test           # 18: classifier, loader contract, patch/manifest consistency, the Host route, module resolution
npm run test:dom   # 33 in headless Chrome over CDP: `:has()`, real Mermaid output, the streaming sequence, both clipboard flavours
```

`test:dom` skips when no Chrome or Chromium is installed.

## Licence

MIT.

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness 用の日本語ネイティブ TUI（設計段階 / design phase）
plugins.readme_text:
# DSH-forJP-TUI

DeepSeek Harness (dsh) のための**日本語ネイティブ TUI**。

> **状態: Phase 0（走路骨格）完了。描画は未着手。**
> 自作バンドルが DSH の Cordis 木に載り、自前の入口（C）から起動し、C が壊れれば
> `dsh --profile` 子プロセス（B）へフォールバックし、`session/event` の生イベントを捕捉できる。
> 検証は `node scripts/verify-bundle.mjs`（12検査）。

## これは何か

dsh の TUI サーフェスを、日本語を第一級に扱う形で自作する。
既存の [dsh-TUI](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI) を参考にしつつ、
コードは共有せず、描画層から自分で設計する。

## 目的

| # | 目的 | 設計要求 |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | 見た目を自分で設計できる | 描画層を自前で握る。装飾演出を既定で入れない |
| P2 | 日本語ネイティブ | 文言を最初からカタログ化。日本語を言語パックに追い出さない |
| P3 | 上流更新で崩れにくい | 依存する上流の非公開契約を最小化し、その数を常時計測する |
| P4 | UX 研究の土台 | UI 層とハーネス層を分離し、UI の反復試行を安くする |
| P5 | 将来ハーネスごと差し替える（思想として保持） | ハーネス境界を1箇所に閉じ込める |
| P6 | ハーネスチューニング研究 | ハーネスの挙動を外から差し替え可能に保つ |

## 確定している方針

- **DSH への載せ方**: in-process の Cordis バンドル（`dsh.bundle.patch`）。承認・ユーザー質問・モデル切替を
  人対話で行うには、これ以外の経路が存在しない（公式 SDK / ACP には承認チャネルが無い）
- **起動**: 自前のフル host-entry を持つ。ただし**失敗時は必ず `dsh --profile` 子プロセスへフォールバック**する
- **描画層**: upstream の [Ink](https://github.com/vadimdemedes/ink) **v8.0.0**（commit `26d2c3f8`）を fork し、
  `src/ink/` に置いて自前で拡張する。Ink 本体はマウス選択・ヒットテスト・スクロール固定を持たないため、
  これらは自作する
- **v0 の範囲**: 入力解析 / 差分描画 / 全角幅 / 入力欄 / ストリーム表示 / ツールカード /
  承認パネル / ユーザー質問パネル / セッション結線 / 中断と終了

## ドキュメント

| 文書 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| [`docs/design/0001-architecture-and-roadmap.md`](docs/design/0001-architecture-and-roadmap.md) | **設計書とロードマップ**（決定ログ D1〜D9、Phase -1〜5、リスク R1〜R8） |
| [`docs/reports/2026-10-18-phase0-walking-skeleton.md`](docs/reports/2026-10-18-phase0-walking-skeleton.md) | **Phase 0 完了レポート**（達成項目・設計を変えた発見・やっていないこと） |
| [`docs/research/2026-10-18-dsh-bundle-authoring.md`](docs/research/2026-10-18-dsh-bundle-authoring.md) | バンドル／Cordis プラグインの書き方（公式実物からの抽出） |
| [`docs/research/2026-10-18-dsh-headless-recipe.md`](docs/research/2026-10-18-dsh-headless-recipe.md) | 公式 `dsh-headless` から抽出したエージェント駆動手順 |
| [`docs/research/2026-10-18-sandbox-and-dsh-home.md`](docs/research/2026-10-18-sandbox-and-dsh-home.md) | 実行環境の制約と `DSH_HOME` 差し替えによる検証方法 |
| [`docs/research/2026-10-18-dsh-integration-surfaces.md`](docs/research/2026-10-18-dsh-integration-surfaces.md) | DSH の統合面・バンドル契約・SDK プロトコル・Ink 反証 |
| [`docs/research/2026-10-18-dsh-core-public-surface.md`](docs/research/2026-10-18-dsh-core-public-surface.md) | DSH 本体の公開インターフェース |
| [`docs/research/2026-10-18-dsh-tui-seam.md`](docs/research/2026-10-18-dsh-tui-seam.md) | 参考実装が DSH とどう接続しているか |
| [`docs/research/2026-10-18-dsh-tui-feature-inventory.md`](docs/research/2026-10-18-dsh-tui-feature-inventory.md) | 参考実装の機能・UX 棚卸し |
| [`docs/research/2026-10-18-renderer-options.md`](docs/research/2026-10-18-renderer-options.md) | TypeScript TUI レンダラ基盤の比較 |
| [`docs/research/2026-10-18-dsh-third-party-tui-web.md`](docs/research/2026-10-18-dsh-third-party-tui-web.md) | DSH と第三者 TUI の外部情報 |

調査ノートには**環境依存のローカル絶対パスをマスク**してある（`$HOME/<workspace>/...`）。

## 開発

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm build
node scripts/verify-bundle.mjs          # 構造検査（A〜D）
COMMANDCODE_API_KEY=... node scripts/verify-bundle.mjs   # 実モデル実行まで（E）
```

検証は `$HOME/.dsh` に**一切書き込まない**。`DSH_HOME` をワークスペース内の `.dsh-home/` に向けて
プロファイルとバンドル解決を完結させる（[理由](docs/research/2026-10-18-sandbox-and-dsh-home.md)）。

入口は `lib/bin.js`（`dsh-forjp`）。環境変数で挙動を切り替えられる:

| 変数 | 値 | 意味 |
|---|---|---|
| `FORJP_ENTRY` | `auto`（既定） | C を試し、失敗したら B へフォールバック |
| | `in-process` | C のみ。失敗したら異常終了 |
| | `child` | B を強制 |
| `FORJP_PROFILE` | 既定 `forjp` | プロファイル名 |
| `DSH_FORJP_HOST_PACKAGE` | 未設定 | ホスト `@deepseek-ai/dsh` のパッケージディレクトリを明示 |

## ライセンス

MIT（[`LICENSE`](LICENSE)）。

fork 元の [Ink](https://github.com/vadimdemedes/ink) も MIT であり、`src/ink/` に取り込む時点で
Ink のライセンス表示を同梱する。

plugins.description: Per-project CodeGraph MCP tools for DeepSeek Harness: each session queries the repo it is actually working in
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-codegraph-project **让 DeepSeek Harness 的每个会话，只查它自己所在仓库的 CodeGraph 索引。** [![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/DeepSeek%20Harness-plugin-5ad1c4)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) [![CodeGraph](https://img.shields.io/badge/CodeGraph-1.6.2%20verified-f0a75a)](https://github.com/colbymchenry/codegraph) [![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-27%20passing-6bc46d)](#验证) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](#license)
--- **这是一个 CodeGraph 兼容层，不是又一个 CodeGraph。** 插件不重新实现任何索引、查询或代码分析逻辑——它直接复用你已经安装的 CodeGraph CLI 和它建好的 `.codegraph/` 索引，把工具按**项目维度**接入 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)。因此： - CodeGraph 升级、换版本、重建索引，本插件照常工作； - Codex、Claude Code、Cursor 等工具的 CodeGraph 配置**原样保留**，互不影响——本插件不写任何全局配置文件，不抢注任何 MCP 服务名； - 卸载本插件，你的 CodeGraph 环境和你其他工具的集成完全不受影响。 接入后，DSH 里的每个会话根据自己的工作目录自动定位 `.codegraph/` 索引，多项目各用各的连接，互不串味。 ## 传统接法的问题：一个 cwd，多个仓库 把 CodeGraph 接进任何宿主（包括 DSH），官方姿势都是配一个 MCP 服务、指向一个项目目录。这在单仓库下没有问题，但 DSH 的插件配置是 **profile 级（全局）**——你只有一个配置位，却可能同时开着五六个仓库的会话： ```yaml - insert: - id: mcp-codegraph name: "@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client" config: cwd: D:\path\to\only-one-project # ← 换个项目就错了 ``` 后果不是报错，而是更糟的**静默查错仓库**——你在仓库 B 的会话里提问，它返回仓库 A 的结果。会话看起来一切正常，答案却是另一个代码库的，直到某天你发现它引用了一个根本不存在的类。 本插件解决的问题就一句话：**让"当前项目"由会话自己决定，而不是由一份全局配置决定。** ## 解法：把"项目"补在 DSH 侧 ``` agent A（仓库甲的会话）── mcp__codegraph__codegraph_explore ──→ ProjectHub(甲) ──→ codegraph 进程 #1 agent B（仓库甲的会话）── mcp__codegraph__codegraph_explore ──→ （共享 #1） agent C（仓库乙的会话）── mcp__codegraph__codegraph_explore ──→ ProjectHub(乙) ──→ codegraph 进程 #2 agent D（无索引目录） ──（看不到任何 codegraph 工具） ``` 三条核心机制： 1. **工具注册在会话 scope 上** —— `agent.ctx.tools.register()`。无索引的会话根本看不到工具，不需要运行时拒绝。 2. **每个项目一个子进程** —— 进程 `cwd` 就是项目根，查询不需要额外参数；同项目的多个会话共享一个进程（引用计数，归零才关）。 3. **子进程走 `ctx.subprocess`** —— 由 DSH 托管，插件停用或 harness 退出时进程一定被回收。 挂载由一个会话级 `agent/pre-step` 监听器持续对齐，因此同时覆盖：会话中途 `codegraph init`（下一条消息即可用）、中途 `cd` 到另一个仓库（工具跟随切换）、索引被删除（工具消失）。 ## 安装 **前置条件** - DeepSeek Harness（`0.2.1-rc.2` 已验证） - [CodeGraph CLI](https://github.com/colbymchenry/codegraph) 已全局安装（`codegraph` 在 PATH 上，或配置 `codegraphBin`） - 目标项目执行过 `codegraph init` **两种安装方式** ```bash # 方式一：从 npm 安装（推荐，装完即用） dsh plugin --profile <你的 profile> add dsh-codegraph-project # 方式二：本地目录（开发/自用） # 在 DSH 的 Plugins 页粘贴本仓库的绝对路径，或用 CLI： dsh plugin --profile <你的 profile> add <本仓库路径> ``` > **两种方式的差异**：从 npm 安装时，依赖（`@deepseek-ai/schemastery`）随包自动 > 就位，无需任何额外步骤；本地目录安装时，由于 ESM 从源码目录解析依赖，需要先在 > 仓库里执行一次 `npm install --omit=dev`。 包已发布：[npmjs.com/package/dsh-codegraph-project](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-codegraph-project) · 当前版本见 `npm view dsh-codegraph-project version`。 安装后**零配置**：有索引的会话自动获得工具，没有的会话干净如初。 ## 配置 所有配置都有默认值，通常不需要动。在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里覆盖： ```yaml - id: codegraph-project config: serverName: codegraph # 工具命名空间 toolCallTimeoutMs: 60000 # 单次调用超时 watchIntervalMs: 2000 # 无索引会话的重探间隔 ``` | 字段 | 默认值 | 说明 | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `true` | 总开关；`false` 时不注册工具、不起进程 | | `serverName` | `codegraph` | 公开工具名为 `mcp____` | | `codegraphBin` | `''` | 可执行文件绝对路径；留空从 PATH 探测 | | `codegraphArgs` | `['serve', '--mcp']` | 配合 `codegraphBin` 的参数 | | `toolCallTimeoutMs` | `60000` | 单次工具调用超时（必须为正数） | | `connectTimeoutMs` | `5000` | MCP 握手超时 | | `watchIntervalMs` | `2000` | 无索引会话的重新探测间隔，`0` 表示每条消息都探测 | **Windows 的 `.cmd` 坑**：npm 全局安装的 `codegraph` 是 `.cmd` 批处理，不能直接 spawn。插件会自动从 npm 全局布局推导 `node.exe` + 入口脚本；推导失败时错误信息里 给出可直接粘贴的 `codegraphBin` / `codegraphArgs` 配置。 ## 认领规则：什么时候一个目录算"项目" 会话目录向上逐层查找 `.codegraph/`，四条边界规则防止"静默服务错误仓库"： | 规则 | 原因 | |---|---| | `.codegraph/` 里必须有 `*.db` | 只有 `daemon.pid` / `daemon.log` 的目录不是项目 | | 遇到 `.git` 就停 | 索引在仓库边界之上属于别的仓库 | | 家目录 / 文件系统根不算 | 否则 `~/.codegraph/` 会让 `$HOME` 下所有会话认领它 | | `.codegraph` 读不了就停 | 继续向上会把权限问题变成查错仓库 | ## 验证 ```bash npm install --omit=dev # 先装依赖（见上） node --test test/locate.test.js test/pool.test.js test/bridge.test.js # 27 个单元测试 node scripts/check-locate.mjs # 认领规则 + 真机抽查 node scripts/check-sharing.mjs <有索引的项目目录> # 同项目共享一个进程 node scripts/check-failure-reporting.mjs # 启动失败的去重上报 node scripts/probe.mjs <有索引的项目目录> <查询词> # 真实 CodeGraph 端到端 node scripts/acceptance.mjs # 真机验收（headless） ``` 部分脚本接受环境变量指定本机测试项目： | 变量 | 用于 | 默认 | |---|---|---| | `CODEGRAPH_TEST_PROJECT` | `check-sharing.mjs`、`acceptance.mjs` | `.` | | `CODEGRAPH_TEST_PROJECTS` | `check-locate.mjs`（逗号分隔多个） | 跳过真机抽查 | | `DSH_BIN` | `acceptance.mjs`（dsh CLI 路径） | Windows 默认安装位置 | `acceptance.mjs` 会临时把插件与探针装进 `headless` profile、跑完自动还原；它验证 Host 内部可观察状态（会话可见工具、进程事实），不跑模型轮次。 ## 诊断 DSH 的 `SubprocessHandle` 不暴露 pid，插件改用**项目标识**对应进程与日志： - 每个 codegraph 子进程带环境变量 `DSH_CODEGRAPH_PROJECT=<项目根>`，按环境变量反查进程即可； - `ProjectHub.projectTag` / `ProjectHub.stderrTail` 暴露同一标识与子进程 stderr 尾部； - 会话销毁时按 debug 级记录释放结果与剩余会话数； - 启动失败在同一项目上只告警一次，恢复后复发会再次告警。 ## 更新 已通过 npm 安装后，升级到新版本： ```bash dsh plugin --profile <你的 profile> add dsh-codegraph-project # 重新 add 即升级到 latest ``` 维护者发布新版本： ```bash # 改代码 → 测试 → 提交（npm version 要求工作区干净） npm test git add -A && git commit -m "..." # 升版本号（同时改 package.json + 自动 commit + 打 tag） npm version patch # 修 bug：0.1.0 → 0.1.1 npm version minor # 新功能：0.1.0 → 0.2.0 npm version major # 破坏性变更：0.1.0 → 1.0.0 git push && git push --tags npm publish --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org ``` 版本号遵循 [semver](https://semver.org/lang/zh-CN/)：已发布的版本号永不复用，改动再小也发新版本号。 ## 文档 | 文档 | 内容 | |---|---| | [docs/implementation-plan.md](docs/implementation-plan.md) | 开发指南：架构、逐模块实现、实施顺序、验收清单 | | [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) | 7 个关键设计决策与被否决的替代方案 | | [docs/technical-findings.md](docs/technical-findings.md) | 12 项 DSH 源码调研与运行时验证记录 | | [docs/risks.md](docs/risks.md) | 13 项风险与边界条件 | | [docs/why-no-prompt.md](docs/why-no-prompt.md) | 为什么不注入提示词 | ## 与 troytse/dsh-plugin-codegraph-project 的差异 参考过 [troytse/dsh-plugin-codegraph-project](https://github.com/troytse/dsh-plugin-codegraph-project)（MIT），设计取舍不同： | 能力 | 它 | 本插件 | |---|---|---| | CodeGraph 来源 | npx 拉取 + 版本管理 | 用系统已安装的 | | 工具注册 | 全局 + guard + 路由 | 按会话 scope | | 索引发现 | 250 行轮询 | `agent/pre-step` 懒检测 | | 提示词 | 注入 usage guidance | 不注入 | | 规模 | ~2900 行 | ~960 行 | ## License MIT

plugins.description: A portable memory protocol for AI agents — load it as standing rules; a curation discipline + reference spec + optional cap hook.
plugins.readme_text:
**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

# Engramory

[![CI](https://github.com/tinqiao-oss/engramory/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/tinqiao-oss/engramory/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Python 3.9+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.9%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/)

**An opinionated, zero-infrastructure memory *protocol* for small-scale, local,
file-based agent memory** — a strict curation discipline plus a validator
(`tools/engramory_doctor.py`), loaded as **standing rules** (`CLAUDE.md` /
`AGENTS.md` / your host's rules file). It is not a database, a framework, or a
relevance-loaded skill. Memory is a folder of small, human-readable markdown files
plus one always-loaded index. No database, no embeddings, no server — just
plain-text files you can open, read, edit, and diff in any editor (the live store
itself stays git-ignored).

> *Engramory* — coined from *engram* (the physical trace a memory leaves in the
> brain) + *memory*. Here: one file = one fact.

> ⚠️ **Unrelated projects share this name.** *engram + memory* is an obvious
> coinage and at least one other repository arrived at it independently. This
> project is only ever `tinqiao-oss/engramory` (npm: `dsh-engramory`); a same-named
> repo under a different owner is not a fork, a mirror, or a newer version of it.

> 🤖 **Are you an AI agent, asked to install or check this?** Start at
> **[AGENT-SETUP.md](AGENT-SETUP.md)**, not at the install steps below. It is the
> procedure for working out what your host can actually enforce, whether a store
> already exists, what you must not touch, and what to tell the user — the parts
> agents reliably get wrong when improvising.

> **Status: 0.12.1 — experimental.** The hard index cap (a `PreToolUse` hook) is
> deterministic for the matched direct-edit tools (`Edit | Write | MultiEdit`) but
> NOT a global write guard (shell tools — Bash, PowerShell, a background Monitor
> command — plus MCP file tools, external editors, and sync clients bypass it);
> the discipline loads as standing rules the model follows, so it's
> best-effort, not guaranteed on every task (see [SKILL.md](SKILL.md) §8). Assumes a
> single writer / serialized writes. Don't rely on it as a "mandatory, reliable,
> cross-agent" memory layer yet.

---

## What this is — and is NOT

Engramory is **not a new memory architecture**. The "markdown files + a small index
loaded into context + the model curates it" pattern is now the mainstream shape
for agent memory, and it ships in several places already. Engramory stands on:

- **Claude Code native auto-memory** — the same markdown-`MEMORY.md`-index +
  lazy detail-file pattern; its system prompt even uses the same
  `user | feedback | project | reference` type vocabulary (per
  [anthropics/claude-code#58840](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/58840);
  the *public docs* describe only the index + topic files). Engramory is a
  disciplined superset of this default.
- **[basic-memory](https://github.com/basicmachines-co/basic-memory)** — markdown
  source-of-truth, YAML frontmatter `type`, `[[wikilink]]` graph, local-first.
- **[obsidian-second-brain](https://github.com/eugeniughelbur/obsidian-second-brain)**,
  **[claude-memory-compiler](https://github.com/coleam00/claude-memory-compiler)**
  ("a loaded index beats vector search at personal scale"), and the broader family
  of markdown-memory skills.

What Engramory contributes is the **opinionated bundle + the discipline**, not the
primitives. Do not claim novelty on markdown, frontmatter, wikilinks, a loaded
index, one-file-per-fact notes, or curation hygiene — all are prior art.

## What's actually differentiated

1. **A role/purpose ontology, headed by `feedback` = procedural memory.** The
   semantic / episodic / **procedural** split is established prior art — the CoALA
   taxonomy, and a named procedural type in LangMem and mem0 — so Engramory does not
   claim the category. What it does is make procedural `feedback` the *spine* of a
   deliberately tiny, hand-authored, human-readable set, with required **Why:** /
   **How to apply:** lines, instead of auto-extracting it into a vector/graph store.
   The contribution is the packaging and discipline, not the ontology.

2. **The curation contract as concrete behaviour** the protocol applies (model-followed, not a hard gate): dedup-before-write,
   update-don't-duplicate, delete-when-wrong, and a negative-scope rule ("don't
   store what git/CLAUDE.md/the code already records"). Surveys consistently name
   *modify/delete/forget* as the most under-implemented memory operation — Engramory
   makes it the spine.

3. **A bounded index designed not to silently rot.** The index loads every session and
   Claude Code reads the first 200 lines / 25 KB (documented behavior), so an unbounded index silently
   drops memories off the end. Engramory warns at 150 lines / 20 KB, compacts-or-asks
   before 200 / 25 KB, and ships a hard `PreToolUse` hook backstop (it blocks only
   *growth* past the cap — shrinking/compaction edits always pass). Both the line and
   byte caps apply — whichever is hit first triggers (an index can be under the line
   count yet over on bytes when the lines run long).

   Claude Code has since followed up on this natively: v2.1.186 (released
   2026-06-22) reminds the agent to compact the index when it nears the cap, and
   v2.1.210 (released 2026-07-14) turned an over-cap write into an explicit error
   instead of a silent truncation. Both are after-the-fact alerts, though — the
   write still lands, and entries past the cap stay invisible until someone
   compacts. Engramory's hook denies the write *before* it happens, so a write
   through the matched edit tools never leaves the index over-cap in the first
   place (writes outside them — a shell, an MCP file tool — are not gated; see the
   status note above and SKILL.md §8). The native alerts validate the direction
   and make a welcome second layer — and older versions and other hosts still
   have neither.

## How it compares

| | storage | recall | human-readable | typed ontology | curation discipline | bounded index | infra |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Engramory** | md files | loaded index → open file | ✅ | ✅ role-based (4) | ✅ contract (model-run) | ✅ 150/200 + hook | none |
| CC auto-memory | md files | loaded index → open file | ✅ | ✅ same 4 types | partial (auto) | ~200-line window* | none (built-in) |
| basic-memory | md + SQLite | semantic/FTS search | ✅ | ✅ freeform type | schema + overwrite checks | ❌ (no loaded index) | SQLite + embeddings |
| obsidian-second-brain | md vault | index-first + search | ✅ | folder-typed | ✅ reconcile/lint | partial | none |
| mem0 / Zep | vector/graph DB | semantic | ❌ (DB) | typed (prefs/episodic/proc.; Zep custom) | auto-extract | n/a | DB + embeddings |
| [agentmemory](https://github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory) | SQLite + vector index (+opt. graph) | hybrid BM25+vector (+opt. graph), RRF | ❌ (DB/engine) | ✅ 4-tier lifecycle (work./epis./sem./proc.) | auto (capture + dedup + decay) | n/a | iii engine (local) + opt. embeddings |

Engramory's lane: **minimalism + actionable role typing + curation discipline, zero
infra.** It does *not* try to out-search basic-memory, out-scale mem0, or
out-capture agentmemory — those solve a different problem (auto-capture /
auto-ingest at volume) at a different cost point. agentmemory is the closest
heavyweight foil: also local-first, but it bets on automatic capture (lifecycle
hooks) + hybrid retrieval (BM25 + vectors + optional graph) on a SQLite/`iii`
engine, where Engramory bets on hand-curation + a tiny always-loaded index and
ships no engine at all.

\* Claude Code's [memory docs](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/memory)
document this exactly: *"the first 200 lines of `MEMORY.md`, or the first 25KB,
whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation."* Other hosts
vary, so the window stays configurable via the hook's env vars.

## Where it fits — and the goal

Engramory is a **portable memory *discipline*, not a

plugins.description: Local-only cross-session memory for DSH with system-prompt injection and a Settings page.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-memory-local

Local-only cross-session memory for DeepSeek Harness.

- Agent tools: `memory_remember`, `memory_recall`, `memory_list`, `memory_forget`,
  `memory_inspect`.
- Relevant entries are injected into the system prompt as a bounded local-memory
  block (never as instructions).
- Settings → **Memory** lets you manage project and global memories: add, edit,
  pin, search, delete, and preview the next injection.

## Storage

Default: `~/.dsh/memory/`

- `global.json` — entries shared by all workspaces.
- `projects/<id>.json` — per-workspace entries.
- `index.json` — workspace path → project id.

No network, no embeddings, no cloud. `DSH_MEMORY_DIR` overrides the directory.

## Scope

- Default: project (current workspace).
- `scope: "global"` is opt-in, for stable user preferences that should follow every
  workspace.

## Safety

- Explicit writes only; conversations are not captured automatically.
- Credential-looking content (`npm_`, `ghp_`, `github_pat_`, `sk-`, Bearer) is
  rejected.
- Content is capped at 4 KiB; injection is capped at 8 entries / 2000 characters.
- `memory_forget` and `memory_inspect` are first-class; deletion is explicit.

## Install

```powershell
# install the local checkout into a profile
plugin_manager install_bundle <absolute path to this directory>
```

Then open Settings → Memory; the page is registered through `settings.section`.

## Notes

The Client half requires `@deepseek-ai/dsh-typert-protocol` for the Host↔Client
Remote bridge. The Host half remains usable without the settings page.

plugins.description: Runtime evidence that helps agents trace, profile, and burn down hotspots in application and native code, GPU kernels, and inference stacks.
plugins.readme_text:
flameox

Bounded local runtime evidence for coding agents.

Flameox coordinates profilers, benchmark tools, trace processors, and direct local targets. It turns an explicit artifact or command into bounded evidence while keeping durable preservation optional. The agent chooses hypotheses and experiments; Flameox records observed inputs, execution provenance, typed evidence, coverage, and limitations. There is no workspace to initialize or project configuration to maintain. Pass exact artifact paths to analysis and an explicit argv plus absolute working directory to capture. Flameox does not search parent directories, edit project files, or provide a hosted service. ## Quick start Configure an MCP client with the global setup command: ```console npx flameox@latest setup ``` Setup detects supported clients and asks which configurations to update. For automation, select clients explicitly, for example `--client codex --yes` or `--all --yes`; `--dry-run` reports the paths and actions without writing. Setup preserves unrelated client configuration and does not change project files. See [the npm package guide](npm/README.md) for details. Update existing MCP registrations with: ```console npx flameox@latest update ``` `update --check` reports available updates without changing configuration. Updates preserve each client's provider extras and settings, verify the new environment before changing release pins, and report which clients need a restart or reconnect. Use `--client codex` to select one client, or `--version 0.2.8` to select a specific release, including for rollback. The Python CLI exposes the same `flameox update` command. For direct CLI use, pass exact artifact paths or an explicit command: ```console uvx flameox analyze preview_artifact /absolute/path/to/artifact.json uvx flameox capture --provider direct --cwd "$PWD" -- python benchmark.py ``` To launch the stdio MCP server manually: ```console uvx flameox mcp serve ``` For local development, clone the repository, install its development dependencies, and inspect the available tools: ```console git clone https://github.com/morluto/flameox.git cd flameox uv sync --extra dev --extra memory --extra trace --extra cpu uv run flameox mcp inspect ``` ## Evidence and storage Analysis and unpreserved capture use bounded session scratch. Session `analysis_id` values expire when evicted or when the server stops. Explicit preservation creates the user-level Flameox data directory and stores native bytes and a canonical evidence bundle by SHA-256. Set `FLAMEOX_DATA_DIR` to choose another location. Preservation is optional; it does not imply full console-output retention. Flameox distinguishes observed, derived, and inferred claims. Profiles guide exploration but do not establish causality or performance improvement. Confirmatory claims require representative workloads, declared metrics and estimands, compatible identities, preserved samples, and a semantic oracle. ## MCP The MCP server has no workspace binding. It exposes named analysis and capture tools through the same operation registry as the CLI. Analysis tools accept explicit sources; capture tools accept a typed target and provider. Tool schemas expose operation-specific fields directly. Inspect the catalog with `flameox mcp inspect`; use `--tool TOOL_NAME` for focused schemas and examples. The complete contract and current tool catalog are in [the interface guide](docs/interfaces.md). Tools return their full bounded results inline, including failures and recovery actions. Preserved evidence has a durable `evidence_id`; `inspect_evidence` returns its redacted metadata and replay sources inline. Capture takes argv, not a shell string. A direct target supplies an absolute working directory and bounded environment overrides. Results may include `next_page`; replay its named analysis tool and arguments unchanged. Capture continuations read collected artifacts and do not rerun the target. MCP work belongs to the live request, so cancellation applies directly and no detached job survives a restart. ## Documentation - [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) describes process and package boundaries. - [Storage and evidence](docs/storage-and-evidence.md) defines preservation and provenance. - [Investigations](docs/investigations.md) covers experiments, comparison, and evidence quality. - [Adapters](docs/adapters.md) documents provider compatibility and integration policy. - [Runtime safety](docs/runtime-safety.md) covers limits, recovery, integrity, and privacy. - [Interfaces](docs/interfaces.md) defines CLI and MCP contracts. - [Testing](docs/testing.md) describes test selections and known proof gaps. ## Development Flameox requires Python 3.12 or newer and uses the committed `uv.lock`. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for development setup and contribution guidance. ```console uv run ruff check src tests tools uv run ruff format --check src tests tools uv run mypy src tests tools uv run pytest -q ``` Flameox is licensed under the MIT License.
